As a member of the library's leadership team, the Director contributes to strategic planning, organizational effectiveness, policy development, change leadership, and cross-campus collaboration in support of the University's research, teaching, and learning mission.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Provide long-range strategic leadership for Access Services by applying systems thinking and leading organizational change to align services with institutional and library priorities. Advance service innovation, policy development, emergency planning and response, and organizational effectiveness in response to evolving research needs, user expectations, and scholarly communication trends.
Direct core operations including circulation,resource sharing, course reserves, stacks management, service desks, and patron services. Ensure reliable, equitable, and continuous access to collections across physical, digital, and remote environments.
Lead administration and optimization of integrated library systems (ILS/LSP) and related access technologies (e.g., Alma, ILLiad, etc.). Partner with Digital Services to enhance discovery, fulfillment, resource sharing, and user access through automation and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled workflows.
Ensure Access Services policies and operations comply with copyright, privacy, accessibility, and other applicable laws, regulations, and institutional policies.
Design and lead assessment strategies using qualitative and quantitative data to evaluate collection assessment projects, service effectiveness, user experience, and operational performance. Use assessment findings to drive continuous evaluation and improvement, planning, decision-making, and leadership reporting.
Develop and manage departmental budgets, staffing models, and resource allocation. Identify efficiencies and align financial, technological, and human resources with strategic service priorities.
Supervise professional staff and student employees. Lead recruitment, training, performance management, and professional development while fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and change-ready workplace culture.
Partner with academic units, IT, student services, and administrative departments to enhance user experience. Represent the library in consortial, regional, and national initiatives related to access services and resource sharing.
Contribute to library leadership governance and strategic initiatives. Engage in professional organizations, scholarship, presentations, and service, with emphasis on advancing access services in research library contexts.

jobs.title: Co-Chair and Open-Rank Faculty Position of Playwriting Program
jobs.institution: Yale University: David Geffen School of Drama at Yale
jobs.description:
David Geffen School of Drama (DGSD) at Yale University seeks an experienced and dynamic theatre practitioner to lead a pre-eminent MFA program in Playwriting.
The Geffen School, in partnership with Yale Repertory Theatre (YRT), trains and advances leaders in the practice of every theatrical discipline, making art to inspire joy, empathy, and understanding in the world. DGSD’s and Yale Rep’s core values are artistry, belonging, collaboration, and discovery: working together as a medical school and teaching hospital might, our community comprises eight three-year MFA programs—Acting, Design, Directing, Dramaturgy and Dramatic Criticism, Playwriting, Stage Management, Technical Design and Production, and Theater Management—as well as a one-year Technical Internship program.
DGSD is committed to the development of a robust theater landscape and makes access a priority: all students in degree and certificate programs receive 100% tuition remission.
The Co-Chair of the Playwriting program reports to the Dean of DGSD and, in collaboration with the Co-Chair, supervises all activities of the Playwriting Program, as well as teaching classes and serving as a mentor to students. In addition to offering classes in the craft, the Playwriting program produces projects for each year’s cohort in which they collaborate with students from other disciplines in the school: New Play Lab (first year), Langston Hughes Festival (second year), and the Carlotta Festival (third year).
RESPONSIBILITIES
Teaching and Mentoring
1. Establish curriculum and class schedule, balancing pedagogical needs with budgetary constraints as well as faculty and space availability.
2. Teach two (2) courses in each of the fall and spring semesters.
3. Oversee quality of teaching; participate in review of faculty. Ensure ongoing student review and evaluation.
4. Conduct script analysis tutorials and production-oriented tutorials with playwriting students for New Play Labs, Langston Hughes Festival, and Carlotta Festival productions as needed.
5. Establish and communicate departmental expectations and requirements to playwriting students. Support, guide, encourage and evaluate their progress.
6. Foster DGSD connections to field resources and promote career placement for playwriting students and alumni.
7. Promote a culture of mutual respect, collaboration, and inclusion.
8. Other duties as requested by the Dean.
Program Administration
1. Collaborate with DGSD Deans and Chairs to determine strategy and policy.
2. Determine and implement student recruitment strategy and process. In concert with Playwriting Program faculty, participate in selecting incoming class, including but not limited to, reading scripts, conducting interviews, prioritizing top choices and alternates, following up with admitted students concerning site visits and matriculation.
3. Hire faculty, including but not limited to, conducting searches, interviews, setting up and observing demonstration classes, calling references. In concert with the Dean and Associate Dean/Managing Director establish salaries; negotiate salaries.
4. Select, contract, and supervise Lecturers, visiting faculty, and workshop leaders.
5. Determine, oversee, and monitor Playwriting Program budget and departmental work-study assignments.
6. Collaborate with the Student Labor Supervisor on all work-study related matters.
7. Collaborate with Managing Director’s Office and Casting Director to hire guest artists for the Workshop with Actors course, as well as for other projects, as necessary.
8. Serve as the central coordinator and information point for DGSD departments on the work of the playwrights and all aspects of the department.
9. Handle requests for information about the program from prospective faculty, students, and the field, as well as recommendations for students and graduates as appropriate.
10. Represent Program and serve as primary department liaison and expert resource for DGSD, Yale, and the field.
11. Other related duties as requested by Dean.
Production Supervision
1. Supervise script selection and development of student plays.
2. Work closely with Dean and Chairs of Directing, Dramaturgy, and Technical Design and Production Programs on scheduling and selection of Playwright/Director/Dramaturg teams.
3. Work closely with Dean and Chair of Acting Program on casting of Langston Hughes Festival and Carlotta Festival Productions.
4. Work closely with Design Program Advisors on the development of designs for Carlotta Festival Productions.
5. Coordinate industry outreach, travel, and accommodations for the Carlotta Festival.
6. Monitor Carlotta Festival marketing copy, proofread marketing materials, and contribute to creating copy as required.
7. Promote and champion Carlotta Festival plays with agents, national and local theatres, and new play development centers.
RANK AND TERM OF APPOINTMENT
The appointment will be at an open rank commensurate with the successful candidate’s experience (Assistant Professor Adjunct/Associate Professor Adjunct/Professor in the Practice), for a term of no less than three years beginning July 1, 2027, renewable, and includes competitive salary with full faculty benefits. Minimum base salary: $110K.
Plus an administrative supplement of $15K tied to the role of Co-Chair.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Probability: 21SAS-210600-MTH- FY27-1008
jobs.institution: University of Rochester: Mathematics
jobs.description:
The Department of Mathematics at the University of Rochester invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in probability, broadly construed. We seek outstanding early-career candidates with a PhD in pure or applied mathematics, statistics, or a related field by the beginning of the appointment, and a record of excellence in research and teaching. This appointment will strengthen the department’s research in probability and support interdisciplinary collaborations aligned with the University’s Boundless Possibility strategic plan.
We welcome candidates working across all areas of probability, with particular interest in applications and connections with other areas of mathematics, applied and theoretical sciences, and engineering.
We especially encourage applications from candidates whose research connects with areas of current University strengths and planned growth. Opportunities include interactions with physics through statistical mechanics, complex systems, and random networks; biology through mathematical evolutionary genetics and stochastic models of biological systems; brain and cognitive sciences through probabilistic models of neural activity, learning, and cognition; computer science and data science through the mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence and machine learning; and economics, political science, and business through stochastic modeling, game theory, and decision making under uncertainty. These examples are not exhaustive.
The successful candidate will be expected to develop a strong independent research program, contribute actively to the department’s research community, and pursue productive collaborations within the department and across the University.
We also seek an enthusiastic teacher and mentor who will contribute to the department’s undergraduate and graduate programs, support students from a broad range of disciplines, and advance the University’s educational mission.
The University of Rochester is a private, R1 research university located in upstate New York. The mathematics department has a tradition of strength in both research and teaching. Current research areas include mathematical physics, ergodic theory, probability, algebra and number theory, analysis, combinatorics, geometry, and topology. The department has a strong undergraduate program, offering BS and BA degrees in mathematics (both with research honors options), a BS in applied mathematics, and a joint BS degree in mathematics and statistics. There are also certificate programs in operations research and actuarial studies.
Rochester is located on Lake Ontario and close to the Finger Lakes region, providing excellent living and recreational opportunities spanning all four seasons. The university is home to the world-famous Eastman School of Music and the Memorial Art Gallery, contributing to a community with a rich arts, music, and entertainment culture.
Questions concerning this position can be addressed to Prof. Doug Ravenel, chair of the search committee, or Prof. Maria Gordina, chair of the Department of Mathematics.

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Physiology and Multi-domain Integration

jobs.description:

Working with Prof. James Higham, a Research Scientist will coordinate the analysis of physiological biomarkers from blood, urine, and feces, and will integrate these measures with data from other aging domains (e.g. omics, morphological, social, perception, organ system) for analysis and publication. The Research Scientist will also be responsible for helping the PI ensure that all grant deliverables and milestones are being met and will help to ensure compliance across the different NYU components of the project. The position is available immediately, but later start dates are potentially negotiable. The position is for one year, renewable for up to five years. jobs.title: Post-Doctoral Associate, Somatic Health and Aging
jobs.institution: New York University: Anthropology Department
jobs.description:
Three positions are available in the New York University Department of Anthropology for a longitudinal study of the rhesus macaques of Cayo Santiago, Puerto Rico, as part of a new U19 award from the National Institute on Aging. All positions are initially for one year, potentially renewable for up to five years.
Post-Doctoral Associate 1 (Area: somatic health and aging)
A Post-Doctoral Associate will focus on variation in whole-animal health and function across the lifespan, using measures of body composition and mobility to understand how social, environmental, and life-history factors shape the living phenotype. This PDA will work closely with Prof. Cassandra Turcotte, University of Calgary, in addition to Profs. James Higham, Susan Antón and Scott Williams at NYU. The PDA will utilize and further develop the CBRU’s long-term somatoskeletal databank, with particular emphasis on integrating DEXA-based measures of body composition with quantitative assessments of mobility and physical function. Together, these approaches provide an opportunity to investigate how individuals differ in growth, condition, functional capacity, and aging, and how these differences are shaped by their social and ecological environments. The position offers extensive opportunities to lead and collaborate on multiple ongoing and planned research studies, develop a distinctive area of research expertise, and engage in national and international dissemination of findings through publications and conferences. The PDA will be required to spend time at the Cayo Santiago field station supervising the collection of movement data, and at both the Cayo Santiago and Sabana Seca Field Stations during the annual trapping period, during which they may be required handle animals. The position is available immediately, but later start dates are potentially negotiable. The position is for one year, renewable for up to five years.
Key Responsibilities
Oversee the collection of whole-animal health, body composition, and functional mobility data.
Work with existing longitudinal anatomical, morphometric, and life-history data.
Establish DEXA imaging as a standardized component of the field research protocol for assessing body composition and somatic condition.
Expand quantitative mobility and kinematic data collection to characterize functional variation across age, sex, social status, and environmental context.
Integrate body composition, mobility, and existing life-history data to investigate variation in somatic health, functional capacity, and aging.
Contribute to the preparation of grant applications and peer-reviewed manuscripts.
Present research findings at academic conferences and institutional meetings.
This position is based in New York and the selected candidate will be expected to work onsite as of their effective start date.
We welcome applications from international candidates; however, please note that NYU is not an E-Verify employer and therefore unable to support STEM OPT extensions.
In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $60,000-65,000 per year. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) the specific grant funding and the terms of the research grant when extending an offer.

jobs.title: Post-Doctoral Associate, Osteology, Health, and Aging
jobs.institution: New York University: Anthropology Department
jobs.description:
Three positions are available in the New York University Department of Anthropology for a longitudinal study of the rhesus macaques of Cayo Santiago, Puerto Rico, as part of a new U19 award from the National Institute on Aging. All positions are initially for one year, potentially renewable for up to five years.
Post-Doctoral Associate 2 (Area: Osteology, health, and aging)
The PDA will focus on variation in skeletal health and morphology across the lifespan, assessing indicators of skeletal health and aging to understand how social, environmental, and life-history factors shape the adult skeletal phenotype. Working closely with Prof. Susan Antón, and in collaboration with Profs. Cassandra Turcotte (University of Calgary), Scott Williams, and James Higham, the PDA will utilize and further develop systematic skeletal collections housed at NYU (the CPRC-NYU collection) and the CBRU’s long-term somatoskeletal databank, with a focus on assessing pathological conditions in gross morphology and imaging including quantitative and qualitative assessments of variation, physical age, and health. Together, these approaches provide an opportunity to investigate how individuals differ in growth, condition, functional capacity, and aging, and how these differences are shaped by their social and ecological environments. The position offers extensive opportunities to lead and collaborate on multiple ongoing and planned research studies, develop a distinctive area of research expertise, and engage in national and international dissemination of findings through publications and conferences. The scholar will also have opportunities to develop independent research questions within the broader theme of skeletal variation in health and function. Based in New York, the scholar will also spend sustained time in Puerto Rico and at imaging facilities in the U.S. where they will collect data and imaging, develop and participate in public science programs, and supervise students and may assist with animal handling and maceration. The position is for one year, renewable for up to five years.
Key Responsibilities
Oversee the collection, organization and assessment of imaging (surface and microCT scans) of skeletons across the lifespan from the CPRC-NYU collection.
Participate in the curation and supervision of curation of the CPRC-NYU collection.
Expand and develop gross pathological assessment of bone to characterize health variation across age, sex, social status, and environmental context.
Expand quantitative assessment of microCT imaging of bone health and disease to understand changes in skeletal frailty with age and sex.
Integrate skeletal data with existing somatic, life-history, and health data to investigate variation in skeletal health, skeletal frailty, mortality, and aging.
Establish publicly available training material (virtual imaging and workshops) to support public engagement of science
Work with existing longitudinal anatomical, morphometric, and life-history data collected by the CBRU.
Contribute to the preparation of grant applications and peer-reviewed manuscripts.
Present research findings at academic conferences and institutional meetings.
Aid in the training and mentorship of more junior CBRU members.
This position is based in New York and the selected candidate will be expected to work onsite as of their effective start date.
We welcome applications from international candidates; however, please note that NYU is not an E-Verify employer and therefore unable to support STEM OPT extensions.
In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $60,000-65,000 per year. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) the specific grant funding and the terms of the research grant when extending an offer.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate (Fawzi lab) - PRA 307
jobs.institution: Brown University: Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry (MCB)
jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Research Associate — NMR Spectroscopy and Structural Biology
Department of Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry / Brown University
Principal Investigator: Nicolas Fawzi
Location: Providence, Rhode Island
Position Summary
The Fawzi Laboratory in the Department of Molecular Biology, Cell Biology and Bi9chemistry (MCB) at Brown University invites applications for a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to develop and apply advanced nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy approaches to investigate the structure, dynamics, and molecular mechanisms of biologically important proteins and protein assemblies.
The successful candidate will use solution NMR and related biophysical and biochemical approaches to address fundamental questions in structural biology, molecular interactions, and disease biology. The position offers an opportunity to develop expertise in cutting-edge NMR methodology while applying these techniques to challenging biological systems.
Research Responsibilities
The postdoctoral researcher will:
Design and conduct NMR spectroscopy experiments to characterize protein structure, motions, and molecular interactions.
Apply multidimensional heteronuclear NMR techniques, including backbone and side-chain resonance assignments and structural characterization.
Develop and optimize NMR experiments for challenging, intrinsically disordered, dynamic, or heterogeneous protein systems.
Use NMR relaxation, chemical-shift perturbation, paramagnetic effects, and other approaches to characterize protein dynamics and molecular interactions.
Integrate NMR measurements with complementary biophysical and biochemical methods.
Analyze and interpret multidimensional NMR datasets using appropriate computational and structural-biology approaches.
Contribute to development of new experimental or computational approaches for studying protein conformational dynamics.
Present research at laboratory meetings, conferences, and seminars and publish findings in peer-reviewed journals.
Collaborate with researchers within the Fawzi laboratory and across Brown University and external institutions.
Mentor undergraduate and graduate students as appropriate.
The Fawzi laboratory provides an interdisciplinary environment at the interface of NMR spectroscopy, structural biology, biophysics, and molecular biology. The postdoctoral researcher will have access to modern NMR instrumentation and opportunities to interact with researchers across Brown's biomedical and physical-science communities.
The position is particularly well suited for a scientist interested in using NMR not simply as a characterization tool, but as a quantitative approach to understand how biomolecular structure and interactions give rise to biological function, and how these are disrupted in disease.

jobs.title: SMU 26-27 - Associate or Full Professor of History of the American West and Director of the Clements Center for Southwest Studies
jobs.institution: Southern Methodist University: Dedman College of Humanities and Sciences
jobs.description:
The Clements Department of History at Southern Methodist University invites outstanding applicants for the directorship of the William P. Clements Center for Southwest Studies and a tenured appointment in the History Department at the rank of advanced Associate or early Full Professor. Fields of expertise may include the North American West, U.S. Southwest, U.S.-Mexico borderlands, and/or related fields.
The position offers unparalleled opportunities for research, scholarly community, and teaching. The Clements Center for Southwest Studies, established in 1996, hosts a competitive fellowship program, incisive symposia series, collaborative seminars, and public programming. It also sponsors the David J. Weber book prize with the Western Historical Association. The director will support fellows and emerging scholars, develop collaborative programming, cultivate community, and further enhance the Center's national and international reputation. Candidates should be prepared to advise and direct graduate students and to teach undergraduate and graduate classes in relevant fields.
The successful candidate will benefit from engagement with the Rees-Jones Library of the American West at SMU. The new library, expected to open in Fall 2027, will be home to one of the most significant collections of Western Americana in the country. While the Rees-Jones Collection is focused primarily on the pre-1901 period, DeGolyer’s 20th-century holdings include Western business enterprises and literature, political collections, and the Archives of Women of the Southwest and Mexican history. The Bridwell Library, the Bridwell Press, the Meadows Museum (a leading center in the United States for exhibition, research and education in the arts and culture of Spain), and the Archaeological Research Center offer other opportunities for exploring diverse histories of the West on SMU’s campus.
About the Department:
The Clements Department of History has 15 full-time faculty members—award-winning scholars and several Altshuler Distinguished Teacher professors (the highest teaching recognition on campus). Our faculty teach undergraduate courses that serve history majors and minors, as well as a number of interdisciplinary majors on campus and the university Common Curriculum. The department’s graduate program emphasizes work on the southwestern United States, the West, ethnic Mexicans, U.S. political and diplomatic history, colonial era, and religious history. The department’s centers, the Clements Center for Southwest Studies and the Center for Presidential History, enrich department life with research colloquia, public lectures, and postdoctoral fellowships.
SMU and Dallas:
SMU offers an exceptional setting for a scholar of the American West. SMU is a private, nonsectarian university of about 12,000 students located in University Park, a highly regarded residential community approximately 15 minutes north of downtown Dallas. The University is home to numerous academic centers with which our faculty engage, including the Texas-Mexico Center, the Dallas Institute of Humanities and Culture, the John G. Tower Center for Political Studies, and the Dedman College Interdisciplinary Institute. Our faculty take advantage of opportunities to teach at SMU’s Taos campus and its study abroad programs.
Beyond the University, the Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area offers the cultural resources of one of the nation's largest and most diverse metropolitan regions, while providing close connections to the landscapes, archives, institutions, and communities central to the history of Texas and the American West. Opportunities abound to engage with organizations, institutions, and historical collections throughout the region, including the Dallas Historical Society, the Old Red Museum of Dallas County History & Culture, the African American Museum, the Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza, the Dallas Public Library’s Texas/Dallas History & Archives Division, and the George W. Bush Presidential Library and Museum. The broader North Texas region also offers access to the Kimbell Art Museum, the Amon Carter Museum of American Art, the Sid Richardson Museum, and the National Cowgirl Museum and Hall of Fame, among other institutions with significant collections and programming related to western history and culture.
Learn more about working at SMU here and living in Dallas here: https://www.smu.edu/businessfinance/hr/workingatsmu

jobs.title: Research Associate position, Division of Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Metabolism
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: Perelman School of Medicine - Medicine - Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism
jobs.description:
The Division of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism in the Department of Medicine at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for a Research Associate position in the Academic Support Staff. This appointment will be initially for one (1) year and continuation during that time period and renewal are based on satisfactory performance and availability of funding (limited to three (3) years). Expertise is required in the specific area of nuclear receptor signaling, including PPARα and HNF4α, hepatic lipid metabolism, genetic regulation of metabolism, circadian biology, epigenetic and transcriptomic data analysis, and metabolic disease research using genetically engineered mouse models and advanced genomic approaches. Applicants must have a Ph.D. degree.
Responsibilities may include conducting independent and collaborative research on the role of nuclear receptors, including PPARα and HNF4α, in hepatic lipid metabolism and metabolic disease; analyzing epigenomic and transcriptomic datasets generated from genetically engineered mouse models; investigating mechanisms underlying circadian regulation in the liver and the role of the hepatic vagus nerve in maintaining circadian rhythms; contributing to experimental design, data interpretation, manuscript preparation, and presentation of research findings; and collaborating with laboratory members on related research projects.
The successful applicant will have an opportunity to develop advanced expertise in metabolic disease research, genomic and epigenomic data analysis, circadian biology, and nuclear receptor signaling. The position provides training and mentorship in experimental design, data interpretation, scientific communication, and collaborative research, supporting the individual's long-term career development in academic biomedical research.

Our Ph.D. program in Computational and Applied Mathematics is currently being modernized in light of the rapid changes in our field associated with the development of artificial intelligence and its applications in science and engineering, and the successful candidate will ideally contribute to this process. Besides our traditional undergraduate programs in applied and pure mathematics, the department participates in programs in data science and has launched a new major in mathematical economics. SMU has extensive high-performance computing facilities, which are freely available to all faculty, and a dedicated center for data science and research computing. https://www.smu.edu/provost/odonnell-institute.
SMU seeks bold, curious and creative faculty to position our students for success. We offer the rare confluence of a comprehensive global research institution and a close-knit intellectual enterprise in the liberal arts tradition. Like our hometown of Dallas, our campus is vibrant. Here, innovative thinkers conduct research that has lasting impact and transform big ideas into new products, inventive technology and world-changing solutions. Our welcoming learning community of faculty and nearly 12,000 students in eight schools embraces a world of people and ideas. Come to SMU to think big and do good. Explore SMU at http://www.smu.edu.

jobs.title: Assistant / Associate Professor of Small Animal Primary Care
jobs.institution: The University of Tennessee - Knoxville: Small Animal Clinical Sciences
jobs.description:
The Department of Small Animal Clinical Sciences of the University of Tennessee, College of Veterinary Medicine invites applications for a full-time clinical track faculty position in Small Animal Primary Care. The position is at the Clinical Assistant or Associate Professor level, depending on qualifications and experience.
The missions of the Department are to educate veterinary students and graduate veterinarians to meet the needs of the pet owning public, to provide advanced patient care, and to generate new knowledge in pet health through basic and applied research. Clinical track faculty at the University of Tennessee are expected to participate in teaching, service, and scholarship programs of the College. Responsibilities of the successful candidate will include clinical service and instruction in small animal primary care to DVM students and house officers, didactic program instruction within the preclinical curriculum, and collaboration in clinical discovery or scholarship.
The University of Tennessee Tickle Small Animal Hospital is a comprehensive and fully equipped facility with the expertise needed to provide advanced medical care. Specialty services supported by departmental faculty include: internal medicine, oncology, neurology, soft tissue and orthopedic surgery, dentistry, ophthalmology, dermatology, behavior, radiology, radiation oncology, anesthesiology, nutrition, physical therapy, shelter medicine, zoo, and exotic and avian medicine and surgery. The College also houses a nationally renowned Veterinary Social Work program. Facilities include: nuclear medicine, computerized tomography, MRI, radiation therapy, video endoscopy, laparoscopy, hyperbaric unit, and physical therapy. The hospital provides VECCS Level I emergency and critical care service 24 hours per day, 365 days a year.
The Primary Care clinic serves dogs and cats belonging to students, faculty, and staff of the University of Tennessee and is not open to the general public. Pets are seen primarily for wellness, illness, minor surgery, dentistry, and senior screening. The clinic will soon relocate to a newly constructed, full-service primary care clinic separate from the tertiary referral hospital. The successful candidate will join a collaborative service currently staffed by 3 faculty, 2 technicians, and 1 veterinary assistant. Primary care faculty are also committed to developing and supporting spectrum of care opportunities within our college and community.
The University of Tennessee College of Veterinary Medicine boasts a collegial environment committed to mentoring new faculty to be successful in their academic career. jobs.institution: Vanderbilt University: Biochemistry
jobs.description:
The Department of Biochemistry at Vanderbilt University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor. Candidates are expected to establish a vigorous, externally funded research program and contribute to the education and mentorship of graduate students and postdoctoral trainees. The successful candidate should use innovative approaches to address biomedical problems at the molecular level. jobs.description:

Activities

A candidate's research must be centered in mechanical engineering, and their teaching interests should align with the Department's core educational programs.

jobs.description:
Princeton University (PU) and the Princeton Plasma Physics Lab (PPPL) are searching for an intellectual leader to establish a new interdisciplinary program in the new Princeton Plasma Innovation Center (PPIC). We seek a leader who will broaden PPPL’s research portfolio while concurrently strengthening ties with the University community.
The ideal candidate would articulate a vision for a new experimental research program at the boundary of plasma science and other disciplines. Possible areas of research include materials science, plasma-surface science, applications of plasma to quantum information science, manufacturing, and microelectronics. We anticipate that the successful candidate will establish a new group and laboratory at PPPL, largely in the PPIC, which is currently under construction and scheduled to be completed in 2027.
The successful candidate will hold a tenured appointment in a relevant department at the University as well as an appointment as a Principal Scientist at PPPL. As PPPL is a Department of Energy (DOE) National Laboratory, familiarity with DOE processes and a successful track record of DOE support are important considerations.
Applications must be submitted online at https://apply.interfolio.com/193934 and should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, a research statement, a teaching statement, and contact information for at least three, but no more than five references. Review of applications will begin by December 1, 2026. References will not be contacted until later in the process. This position is subject to the University's background check policy.
All inquiries will be treated confidentially within the committee and should be addressed to Lyman Page, Dept of Physics, Princeton University, page@princeton.edu.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Position in Dr. Michael J. Betenbaugh's Lab
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
jobs.description:
Are you excited to tackle unsolved challenges in filamentous fungal biotechnology and biomanufacturing? Join Michael Betenbaugh’s research lab to develop and strengthen some of the most in-demand experimental research skills in academia and industry today.
We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled Postdoctoral Researcher to join our dynamic research team. The successful candidate will lead an experimental project focused on improving filamentous fungi as platforms for the production of valuable biomolecules. The research will combine fungal cultivation, strain engineering, molecular biology, bioprocess development, and advanced analytical techniques to identify and overcome biological and process bottlenecks. A Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Biological Sciences, Bioengineering, Biotechnology, Microbiology, or a related field is desired.
Johns Hopkins offers an outstanding environment for life sciences research, with a dynamic community spanning biomolecular engineering, biophysics, biochemistry, microbiology, and medicine.
Standard Johns Hopkins employee benefits.
Baltimore is one of the most affordable and livable cities on the US East Coast.
The Betenbaugh Laboratory offers extensive opportunities to collaborate with industrial partners across the biopharmaceutical and biotechnology sectors.
Become part of the AMBIC biomanufacturing center, directed by Prof. Betenbaugh, and participate in AMBIC conferences, workshops, and seminars.
Laboratory alumni have advanced to positions at major companies, including Genentech, Merck, Pfizer, and GSK, as well as emerging startups such as Drūl and Biolinco.
The initial appointment period is one year, with the expectation of two or more years in total.
Supportive mentoring environment with regular one-to-one meetings with Dr. Betenbaugh.
More information about the Betenbaugh Lab is available at https://www.betenbaughlab-jhu.com/.
Key responsibilities may include:
Conduct literature reviews on filamentous fungal biology, strain engineering, fermentation, and biomanufacturing technologies.
Design and perform experiments to improve fungal growth, productivity, product quality, and process robustness.
Culture filamentous fungi in shake flasks and bioreactors and evaluate the effects of media composition and process conditions.
Apply molecular biology and genetic engineering techniques to modify and characterize fungal production strains.
Use analytical methods to quantify growth, substrate consumption, metabolite production, and product yield and quality.
Analyze and interpret experimental data to identify biological and process bottlenecks and guide subsequent experiments.
Prepare and present research findings through journal articles, conference presentations, and internal reports.
Maintain detailed documentation of experimental workflows, results, and methodologies.
Communicate research progress and findings to academic and industrial collaborators.
Assist in mentoring graduate students and junior researchers within the team

jobs.title: Visiting Postdoctoral Fellow in Dr. Michael J. Betenbaugh's Lab
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
jobs.description:
Visiting Postdoctoral Fellow
The Betenbaugh Lab at Johns Hopkins University is seeking a visiting postdoctoral researcher for an eight-week project focused on integrating multiomic data with genome-scale metabolic models of mammalian production cells.
The researcher will develop a standardized computational framework combining fluxomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics to infer how cellular metabolic priorities change across experimental conditions. The framework will be evaluated using CHO cells across growth and production phases and HEK-293 cells under transfected and non-transfected conditions.
Key activities will include:
Integrating multiomic datasets with genome-scale metabolic models
Comparing inferred metabolic priorities across cell lines and process conditions
Developing reproducible code and a tutorial notebook
Presenting findings and contributing to a joint publication
Applicants should hold a Ph.D. in chemical engineering, bioengineering, systems biology, computational biology, or a related field. Experience with metabolic modelling, omics analysis, or mammalian cell bioprocessing is desirable.

Familiarity with text parsing and analysis (natural language processing) and/or machine learning techniques is preferred.
Demonstrated exceptional written and oral communications skills needed – a writing sample is required.

At least 6 months of research experience in a research role as a research assistant during the academic year or a summer internship in a research lab or governmental institution such as the NY Fed.
Bachelor’s degree in Economics or in a quantitative discipline such as Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, with Economics coursework (including the econometrics sequence)

jobs.title: IFANCA Chair of Indian Muslim Studies and Associate Professor
jobs.institution: Arizona State University: School of Historical, Philosophical and Religious Studies
jobs.description:
About the Position
Arizona State University's The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences invites applications and nominations for the inaugural IFANCA Chair of Indian Muslim Studies, at the rank of Associate Professor, with a start date of August 16, 2027. The Chair will hold tenure in the School of Historical, Philosophical, and Religious Studies (SHPRS) and will be fully embedded in the Center of Muslim Experience in the United States (CME-US), ASU's hub for innovative, publicly engaged scholarship on Muslim life in America and globally.
Position Overview
The inaugural IFANCA (Islamic Food and Nutrition Council of America) Chair of Indian Muslim Studies will be a senior scholar — or a highly accomplished scholar on a strong upward trajectory whose work exemplifies both rigorous humanistic inquiry and the capacity to lead. The Chair will advance innovative research in Indian Muslim Studies, shape CME-US's intellectual agenda, and contribute to ASU's commitments to inclusive excellence, global engagement, and meaningful public scholarship.
About the Center of Muslim Experience in the United States (CME-US)
The Center of Muslim Experience in the United States (CME-US) is a multi-partnership, transdisciplinary research and community outreach center at Arizona State University leading the way in producing transformative scholarship about Muslims in the U.S. that contributes to an American inclusive future.
About the School of Historical, Philosophical, and Religious Studies
ASU’s School of Historical, Philosophical, and Religious Studies (SHPRS) is one of the nation’s largest and most innovative transdisciplinary humanities institutions. With 92 faculty and nearly 1,600 majors, the school teaches more than 33,000 students each year in bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs. A substantial portion of the student population is online, including a pioneering master’s program in World War II Studies in collaboration with the National World War II Museum in New Orleans. Additionally, the school hosts transdisciplinary programs and affiliated research and education centers.
About The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences is the academic heart of Arizona State University, committed to improving communities on a local, national and global scale. We support the professional development and growth of our faculty and staff in their cutting-edge research to advance these aims. Within The College, our faculty engage with a large curious student body, guiding them as they grow into socially aware, critical thinkers and writers able to succeed in a wide range of careers and to address the challenges of the twenty-first century. Advancing the success of our students remains our top priority. To learn more about The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, please visit https://thecollege.asu.edu.
About Arizona State University
ASU exemplifies a new prototype for the American public research university. As articulated in the ASU Charter, ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves.
Essential Functions
The successful candidate will be expected to:
The Chair will advance innovative research in Indian Muslim Studies, shape CME-US's intellectual agenda, and contribute to ASU's commitments to inclusive excellence, global engagement, and meaningful public scholarship.
Maintain a distinguished, internationally recognized research and publishing agenda in Indian Muslim Studies within their humanistic discipline
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses aligned with their expertise and in accordance with the curricular needs of the School of Historical, Philosophical, and Religious Studies
Mentor graduate students and junior faculty
Provide intellectual leadership in shaping CME-US's research, programming, and initiatives related to Indian Muslim Studies
Foster interdisciplinary collaboration across ASU, nationally, and internationally
Organize and convene regular conferences, workshops, and seminars
Engage public audiences, community partners, and broader civic life
Supports IFANCA’s mission which includes values of service, adaptability, and integrity and increase awareness through education
Disciplinary Home and Areas of Scholarly Interest
This position is anchored in the Humanities and housed in SHPRS. We particularly welcome scholars working in:
History (including intellectual, social, religious, political, and cultural history)
Religious Studies (anthropology of religion, religious thought, material culture, and contemporary and global religious movements)
Philosophy (including political philosophy, ethics, and philosophy of religion)
Related humanistic fields such as Literary and Cultural Studies, Gender and Justice Studies, Ethnic Studies, Islamic Studies, Asian Studies, or Law and Ethics, where the primary methodology is humanistic
Candidates’ research should focus on Indian Muslim communities in any period (precolonial, colonial, or postcolonial) with attention to contemporary concerns, and may address themes including, but not limited to, pluralism and justice, postcolonial nationalisms, migration and diaspora (with particular attention to Indian Muslims in the United States), law and governance, public narratives and public memory, environmental humanities and ethics, social movements, intellectual history, or everyday lived experience.
Appointment and Support
The IFANCA Endowed Chair comes with a competitive salary, dedicated research funds, and programming support commensurate with rank and experience. The Chair will be fully integrated into CME-US's collaborative environment and is expected to be an active contributor to its mission and community. The position also offers opportunities to collaborate with other ASU centers and initiatives focused on religion and conflict, transborder studies, Asian studies, security studies, and applied ethics.

Directing undergraduate research and senior comprehensive projects and mentoring and advising students.
Contributing to service within the Department and College.

jobs.description:
The Department of Architecture at the University of Virginia School of Architecture welcomes applications for two endowed faculty fellowships. These two-year, non-tenure-track Assistant Professor General Faculty positions support both research and teaching for emerging practitioners, scholars, or architects seeking to expand their body of work and engage in academia. We seek candidates with a transformative vision for architecture, particularly those with cross-disciplinary interests that connect architecture with landscape architecture, urban design, planning, history and theory, or fields beyond the profession, and that address critical issues of our time.
This is a full-time, two-year appointment, with the expectation that the fellows will reside in Charlottesville and actively engage with faculty, staff, and students at the University. Successful candidates must hold a terminal degree in Architecture (MArch) or a comparable degree in a related design field (such as MLA, MUD, PHD). Faculty fellows are expected to develop a research project and teaching and to present the results of their work in the form of an exhibition in the fall of their second year. Fellows are required to teach four courses per year, including two studios, one required course within the school’s core curriculum, and one elective aligned with their area of research. Fellows will also have the opportunity to participate in committees and other faculty administrative duties.
The Department of Architecture's mission is to educate and inspire the next generation of architectural leaders who understand our discipline as inseparable from the landscapes, cultures, environments, and histories in which we are situated. We actively encourage collaboration across the School of Architecture's disciplines, including with the departments of landscape architecture, urban and environmental planning, and architectural history, as well as with the larger university. As a vital member of this vibrant community, the successful candidate will advance these aims through teaching, research, and collaboration with faculty and students.
The Michael Owen Jones and Robertson Fellowships are structured to provide a gateway into academia and support the development of design research and teaching trajectories. The UVA School of Architecture promotes this by encouraging cross-disciplinary collaboration, providing mentorship, and supporting research development within the school and across the university. Fellows have access to library systems and recently renovated studio, shop, and project spaces, providing state-of-the-art facilities for creative work, scholarly inquiry, and collaborative research (https://www.arch.virginia.edu/about/fablab, https://makergrounds.virginia.edu/).

jobs.description:
The Infrastructure and Sustainability group at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) has 1 to 2 openings for the position of Post-doctoral Fellow. The group is taking system-based approaches to understand the environmental sustainability of our cities and the built environment. We are answering how we can improve our urban infrastructure system that better meet the demand while reducing the environmental impacts. Our research is synthesizing interdisciplinary knowledge to improve our understanding of key dynamics governing urban sustainability and offer insights into what should be done on an urban scale to gain more sustainability benefits.
Starting salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Fringe benefits including annual leave, medical and dental benefits will be provided.

jobs.title: Post-doctoral Fellows/Research Assistants
jobs.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology: Division of Environment and Sustainability
jobs.description:
The Division of Environment and Sustainability (ENVR) at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) invites applications and expressions of interest for multiple Research Assistant and Postdoctoral Fellow positions, across three major research areas: Air Quality and Health, Climate Adaptation and Resilience, and Sustainable Economy and Integrated Solutions.
ENVR brings together expertise across environmental science, engineering, health, data science, economics, finance, policy and the social sciences to address complex environmental and sustainability challenges. We are also expanding our capabilities in software development, artificial intelligence and geospatial technologies to support research, education and the translation of research into practical applications.
Air Quality and Health
Our research examines the sources, transport, exposure and health impacts of air pollution, integrating atmospheric observations and modelling with exposure assessment, epidemiology and health-risk analysis. A major objective is to translate scientific understanding into practical information that can better protect public health.
We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in environmental epidemiology, biostatistics, exposure assessment, air-pollution health research and health-risk modelling. Relevant experience may include time-series or cohort analysis, exposure-response relationships, mortality and morbidity analysis, multi-pollutant and compound environmental risks, and integration of environmental, meteorological, demographic and health datasets.
Experience with R and/or Python, statistical modelling, GIS, data analytics and machine learning would be advantageous.
Climate Adaptation and Resilience
Our research addresses the growing risks associated with climate change and extreme weather, spanning high-resolution weather and climate prediction, climate-risk assessment, early-warning systems, and the “last-mile” challenge of translating warnings into effective actions by individuals and communities.
We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas:
Weather and climate modelling: high-resolution regional and urban weather/climate modelling; model development and process improvement; extreme precipitation, tropical cyclones, heat and other high-impact weather; MPAS or comparable modelling systems; HPC, model evaluation and diagnostics, and analysis of large climate datasets.
Climate risk and early warning: climate-hazard and impact modelling; exposure and vulnerability assessment; impact-based forecasting; development and evaluation of early-warning systems.
Last-mile communication and behavioural response: understanding how people perceive, trust, interpret and respond to climate and extreme-weather warnings, and how warnings can be made more personalized, credible and actionable. Relevant expertise may include social and environmental psychology, behavioural science, risk perception, risk communication, decision-making and behavioural intervention design.
Community engagement and implementation: working with NGOs, community organizations and vulnerable or high-risk population groups to co-design, test and evaluate warning messages, communication channels and practical interventions, including whether warnings reach the intended populations and lead to appropriate protective actions.
Candidates may come from atmospheric science, meteorology, climate science, environmental science, engineering, geography, data science, psychology, behavioural science, public health, social science, risk communication or related disciplines. Interdisciplinary candidates who can connect physical climate-risk information with human behaviour and community implementation are particularly encouraged.
Sustainable Economy and Integrated Solutions
Our research develops practical and integrated approaches to decarbonization, sustainable development and climate resilience, bringing together science and technology with economic, financial and policy considerations.
We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas:
Decarbonization and sustainable transport: maritime and other transport sectors, alternative and low-carbon fuels, lifecycle assessment, carbon accounting, and sustainability and certification of fuel pathways.
Biodiversity and nature-based solutions: ecosystem and biodiversity modelling, spatial analysis, assessment of ecosystem services, and evaluation of nature-based approaches to climate mitigation and adaptation.
Climate risk, economics and finance: quantitative climate-risk assessment, sustainable finance, and the use of insurance and other financial mechanisms to support climate adaptation and resilience.
Relevant backgrounds may include environmental science and engineering, energy and transport, economics and finance, operations research, data science, lifecycle assessment, ecology, environmental management and public policy.
Cross-cutting Software, AI and GIS Development
We are also seeking candidates, particularly at the Research Assistant level, with strong computer science and software-development backgrounds to develop next-generation digital tools supporting environmental research, education and public applications.
We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in one or more of the following:
Web and mobile application development, including interactive spatial web applications, mapping, geospatial analytics, data collection, visualization and field applications;
GIS and geospatial computing, including spatial databases, geoprocessing pipelines, mapping and visualization libraries, and tools such as GDAL/OGR, PostGIS and GeoPandas;
AI-assisted software development and applications, including effective use of large language models, generative AI, APIs and AI coding tools to accelerate development and automate research and data workflows;
Scientific visualization and communication, including interactive visualization, time-series visualization, animation and AI-assisted generation of explanatory and educational materials; and
Development of robust, maintainable scientific software, including appropriate documentation, testing, performance optimization and user-interface design.
Candidates should normally have a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science or a closely related discipline, with sound fundamentals in software engineering, algorithms and data structures. Proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript, Python and/or mobile development frameworks such as Flutter, React Native, Swift or Kotlin would be valuable.
Experience with web or mobile application development is particularly desirable. Familiarity with geospatial data and environmental applications is advantageous but candidates with a strong computer science background and an interest in applying their skills to environmental and sustainability problems are also encouraged to apply.

jobs.institution: Pompeu Fabra University: Department of Political and Social Sciences
jobs.description:
Job title
One 6-months Senior Researcher at Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF), Department of Social and Political Sciences, Barcelona, Catalonia.
REFERENCE CALL: CPIS-PSR-2026-21
Offer publication date: 21st, September 2026
The senior researcher will assist Professor Toni Rodon on the project PRISM (Policing, Representation, Identity and Social Mandate)
Deadline to submit applications: 06th, October, 2026
Financing source:
The contract will be funded by the Fundación BBVA—Becas Leonardo de Investigación Científica y Creación Cultural. The Foundation funds the project.
Official number reference: PRISM: Policing, Representation, Identity, and Social Mandate. REF LEO26-1-22892.
Research Line: Public opinion, social identity, policing, political representation
Job description
The researcher will offer support on the PRISM project, which pretends to deepen our understanding of the relationship between police legitimacy and identity, considering both citizens’ and law enforcement agents’ identities and examining the role of mediating factors such as political ideology, education and social class.
The RA will develop several tasks, mainly quantitative, to support the aforementioned projects.
Main tasks: The main tasks for the researcher will be:
1) To clean and analyse aggregate- and individual-level data.
2) To support the PI and the research team designing a survey, and survey experiments.
3) To support the PI and the research team in liaising with the survey company.
4) To support the research team with additional clerical or admin duties.
Requirements:
1. Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in any field (preference for social sciences).
2. High level of fluency in written and spoken English.
3. Advanced knowledge of R, and/or Quarto.
4. Experience working on surveys, and survey experiments.
5. Attention to detail.
Other skills that will be valued
1. Proficiency in Catalan and Spanish (written and spoken).
2. Experience working on topics related to policing
Terms and conditions of the contract
Group: 3n
Part-time position: The contract is part-time and will be for 17.5 hours per week.
Gross annual salary for a 35h contract is: 33407€ approx, which is a monthly gross salary of 2,447€ euros; for a 17.5h contract: gross annual salary: 16 704€ approx
Job Location: Barcelona, Catalonia.
Type of Contract Indefinite according to the provisions of article 23 bis of the Llei 14/2011, from the 1st of June, of science, technology, and innovation.
The labour contract includes all the benefits of the Spanish Public Health and Social Security System.
The estimated start date is the 1st November 2026. The expected duration of the tasks is 6 months, but it could be extended if both parties agree and there are more tasks to be done.
Selection criteria:
Only applications from candidates who fulfil the requirements mentioned above will be evaluated, following these criteria:
● Experience and skills: 1-5 points

● President: Toni Rodon
o Substitute: Martí Rovira
● Secretary: Emanuele Murgolo
o Substitute: Marc Sanjaume

Candidates must pass a minimum of 4 points for each of the selection criteria.
The selection committee will consider the possibility of interviewing candidates who pass the minimum score.

To apply for this position, interested candidates should send the following documentation:

jobs.title: Healey Family Fellow in Irish Writing, Global Irish Studies Initiative
jobs.institution: Georgetown University: Global Irish Studies
jobs.description:
Healey Family Fellow in Irish Writing (Spring 2027 Semester)
The Global Irish Studies Initiative in Georgetown University’s College of Arts and Sciences seeks applications for the Healey Family Fellowship in Irish Writing for the Spring 2027 (January to May, 2027) semester. The Fellowship, established in 2026, invites a writer in any genre (poetry, fiction, creative non-fiction, drama, etc.), who is based in Ireland or whose work deals substantially with Ireland, to spend a semester at Georgetown University.
The Fellow will teach one class (2.5 hours total per week) in literary studies or creative writing practice, and will be based in the Department of English. In addition, the Fellow will offer at least one public event in the course of their tenure, and will be expected to engage with colleagues and students from the Global Irish Studies Initiative, the Department of English, and the wider university.
Georgetown University has a long history of teaching contemporary Irish literature and supporting Irish writers through the Global Irish Studies Initiative, the Lannan Center for Poetics and Social Practice, and the Department of English. The Healey Fellowship extends this tradition of hospitality toward Irish writing in all its forms in the university.
The Global Irish Studies Initiative is committed to research and teaching that reflects the richness and diversity of modern Ireland. As such, we welcome applicants whose life or work exhibits a wide understanding of both Irishness and Irish writing.
Timing of the Appointment:
We intend to appoint one Fellow for the Spring (January to May) 2027 semester.
However, we also welcome applications from those interested in joining us for the Fall 2027, Spring 2028, Fall 2028, or Spring 2029 semesters. We intend to appoint one Fellow in each academic year. Availability of the position from Fall 2027 to Spring 2029 is contingent on funding, and will be at the discretion of the Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences.
Please indicate clearly in your cover letter whether you are applying for Spring 2027 or for a future semester, or both. If for a future semester, please indicate which one(s).
Required Qualifications:
A demonstrated publication history is required. Candidates must show evidence of active and ongoing creative practice and a strong record of publication.
Commitment to fostering an inclusive environment and working with students from diverse backgrounds.
Desired Qualifications:
Experience teaching in a university-level literature or creative writing program.
A record of public engagement through readings, workshops, or other public-facing events.
Remuneration
The projected base salary range is $42,750.46 - $50,389.40 for the fellowship period (January to May, 2027). Compensation is determined by a number of factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s individual qualifications, experience, education, skills, and certifications, as well as the University’s business needs and external factors.
Application Instructions
Click on Apply Now to submit the following required materials:
1. Cover Letter describing your qualifications that match this position
2. CV, including details of publications, public engagement, and teaching (where applicable)
3. One-page description of a class you would like to offer
4. 20-50-page sample of published writing
Materials are due by October 16, and can be submitted through the Interfolio link.
For further information or clarification of any of the details of the position, please contact Dr. Cóilín Parsons: coilin.parsons@georgetown.edu

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Psychology
jobs.institution: The University of Texas at Austin: Department of Psychology
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology at The University of Texas at Austin invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position to begin August 16, 2027. We seek candidates whose work addresses enduring basic science questions of human behavior using cutting-edge methods, with expertise in social or developmental psychology and flexibility regarding the candidate’s specific field of specialization within those areas. Successful candidates will build an externally funded and nationally recognized research program and excel as instructors and mentors, joining vibrant and engaged colleagues from a range of scholarly backgrounds who seek to study behavior across the lifespan, in social context, and in health and disease. This critical mass of expertise is well-situated to provide early-career mentorship and collaborative opportunities for scholars asking foundational questions.
Department faculty have access to the leading supercomputer center in the country (Texas Advanced Computing Center, TACC), the Children’s Research Center with facilities adjacent to the Priscilla Pond Flawn Child and Family Laboratory, a Siemens Prisma 3T scanner, and rich collaborative opportunities with colleagues in Human Development and Family Sciences, School of Computing, Neuroscience, Sociology, and Dell Medical School, among other units. The Department recently launched a new college-wide major in Behavioral and Social Data Science (BSDS), the first undergraduate degree program in the country devoted to producing data-science-ready graduates with a solid understanding of human psychology.
Duties will include developing an independent sponsored research program, collaborating with other faculty from a wide range of backgrounds, mentoring and teaching graduate and undergraduate students, and serving the department, university, and profession.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Literature and Creative Writing (American Literature of the Long 19th Century...)
jobs.institution: Hamilton College: Hamilton College Faculty
jobs.description:
The Literature and Creative Writing Department at Hamilton College invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor, beginning July 1, 2027, to teach American Literature of the long nineteenth century in a hemispheric or trans-oceanic context. We are especially interested in candidates with secondary expertise in Environmental Studies, Disability Studies, or Queer Studies. The position requires institutional service including academic advising of undergraduate students after the first year. We are seeking candidates who can demonstrate their experience in teaching or working with broadly diverse student populations while contributing to a vibrant learning community that values academic freedom, creativity, and intellectual curiosity. Your cover letter should address the ways in which you would enhance the educational experience of students and further the College’s educational goals.
The Literature and Creative Writing Department offers innovative concentrations and minors in creative writing and literatures composed in or translated into English, across temporal and geographical categories. The department, one of the College’s largest, consists of 14 tenured and pre-tenure faculty, who teach and do scholarly and creative work in a wide variety of genres, fields, and forms. We take a broad, intermedial view of literary and cultural inquiry; many of us pursue comparative and interdisciplinary work—engaging, for example, book history, critical media studies, philosophy and intellectual history, sound studies, translation studies, or visual culture studies—from a variety of theoretical perspectives. Because we are a department that both studies and creates literature, we require students within both majors to do work in creative practice as well as literary and cultural analysis. More information about the department, its faculty, and programs can be found at this link.
Candidates with ABD in English or Comparative Literature, although candidates with a Ph.D. are preferred. The teaching load for this position is four courses during the first year and five courses thereafter. The expected 9-month base salary range for this position is $94,500 to $100,400. Candidates should submit a cover letter, c.v., writing sample (20-25 pages), and contact information for three professional references via Interfolio at https://apply.interfolio.com/194044. Questions regarding the search may be directed to Steven Yao, Search Committee Chair, at syao@hamilton.edu. Applications will be accepted until Nov. 1. Our review of candidates will begin on Nov. 2.
Hamilton College is a residential liberal arts college located in central New York. The College has built its reputation on the teaching excellence and leading scholarship of its faculty, and on the academic distinction and intellectual curiosity of its approximately 2000 students who take advantage of Hamilton’s open curriculum (https://www.hamilton.edu/academics/open-curriculum). Accomplished faculty, highly capable and motivated students, and a student-faculty ratio of 9:1 provide an educational experience that emphasizes academic excellence, intellectual and cultural diversity, and respect for differences in the development of students as engaged members of their communities. Hamilton’s commitment to diversity is embodied in its need-blind admission policy for US Citizens and Permanent Residents; furthermore, Hamilton College meets the full demonstrated financial need for all admitted and enrolled students during their four years on campus. Please visit the college website for more information (www.hamilton.edu).
Hamilton College is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating an accessible, supportive environment and an educational experience that recognizes a wide array of experiences, backgrounds and viewpoints as integral components of academic excellence. Candidates who can contribute to those goals are encouraged to apply and identify their strengths in these areas. Applicants with dual-career considerations can find other Hamilton and nearby academic job listings at https://www.hercjobs.org/regions/higher-ed-careers-upstate-new-york/, as well as additional information at https://www.hamilton.edu/dof/faculty-development/resources-for-prospective-or-new-faculty/opportunities-for-spouses-or-partners (Opportunities for Spouses or Partners). Hamilton provides domestic partner benefits.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Psychology (Clinical)
jobs.institution: The University of Texas at Austin: Department of Psychology
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology at The University of Texas at Austin invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Clinical Psychology to begin August 16, 2027.
Our Clinical Psychology program is nationally recognized for high-quality research and clinical science training. Our current faculty conduct research that spans molecular biology to community implementation, with strengths in health psychology (including cognitive aging, eating pathology, and sexual health); anxiety, trauma, and exposure-based interventions; translational intervention science; and psychiatric genetics. We seek candidates whose research programs will complement and build on these strengths, with flexibility regarding the candidate’s specific field of specialization.
The successful candidate will build an externally funded and nationally visible research program, while excelling as an instructor and mentor to doctoral students in our APA- and PCSAS-accredited Clinical Psychology Ph.D. program, and to undergraduate students.
Department faculty have access to the Imaging Research Center and its Siemens Prisma 3T scanner, the Texas Advanced Computing Center (one of the country’s leading supercomputing centers), the clinical program’s in-house training clinic. Collaborative opportunities exist with departmental faculty in other areas, and with colleagues at Dell Medical School, the Waggoner Center for Alcohol and Addiction Research, Neuroscience, and the Population Research Center, among other units. This critical mass of expertise is well-situated to provide early-career mentorship and professional development opportunities.
Duties will include developing an independent sponsored research program, collaborating with other faculty from a wide range of backgrounds, mentoring and teaching graduate and undergraduate students, contributing to clinical supervision and/or training, and serving the department, university, and profession.

jobs.title: Assistant Scientist METRC
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: Department of Health Policy and Management
jobs.description:
The Department of Health Policy & Management at the Bloomberg School of Public Health is seeking an assistant scientist to work with the Major Extremity Trauma Research Consortium (METRC). The successful candidate will serve as a core member of the METRC Coordinating Center, a multi-center collaboration of over 30 civilian and military trauma centers dedicated to conducting the research needed to improve outcomes of service members and civilians who sustain major limb trauma. METRC provides the platform for contributing to the science of conducting clinical research in a challenging patient population and treatment environment. The position includes a combination of administrative and scholarly activities and requires coordination with investigators and staff from multiple departments and institutions.
The Assistant Scientist will manage and coordinate several multicenter clinical trials supported by METRC. Under the direction of the METRC Coordinating Center Director and Deputy Director Director(s), the Assistant Scientist is responsible for writing narratives for new grant submissions, developing research protocols, managing protocol committees, and overseeing site performance, study enrollment and follow-up, data analysis and communication of results. The role is supported by several grants originating from the Department of Defense and National Institutes of Health, but the research portfolio will change over time, and may include projects funded by private industry or PCORI.
Specific Duties & Responsibilities
Function independently and serve as a key contributor to study development and design for several multicenter studies.
Collaborate with faculty to develop proposals for funding, focused on the research priorities of METRC.
Lead development of study protocols and data collection forms. Provide oversight and coordination of protocol committee meetings, piloting data collection, and manage research staff within the coordinating center to deliver training on study procedures to research teams at participating clinical centers.
Manage regulatory approvals, amendments, and annual progress reports for each study in accordance with local IRB and sponsor IRB policies.
Design, review, interpret, and integrate data from reports on enrollment, follow-up, and data quality for assigned studies.
Participate in the analysis and interpretation of study results and drafting study reports and papers.
Provide on-going technical and scientific guidance to the research staff and participating centers.
Serve on consortium working groups or committees as appropriate.
Attend scientific meetings, conferences and training courses to enhance job and professional skills.
