jobs.title: Instructor in Pediatrics (Non-Invasive Imaging) at CUMC
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Pediatrics
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY/POSITION DESCRIPTION
This opportunity to join the Department of Pediatrics at the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons at the rank of an Instructor in Pediatrics in Non-Invasive Imaging is an exciting one. Columbia University Irving Medical Center, one of the nation’s foremost academic health science centers. The Department of Pediatrics at Columbia University Irving Medical Center is the top in comparison with other pediatrics department in the NY region in NIH research funding.
Columbia University Medical Center (CUMC)/Morgan Stanley Children’s Hospital of New York is now accepting applications for advanced fellowship training in non-invasive imaging in the upcoming academic year. Applicants will have completed their general pediatric cardiology fellowship training at an accredited ACGME institution prior to the start date of July 1st will be considered. The Pediatric Non-Invasive Imaging Laboratory at Columbia University Irving Medical center is one of the largest imaging programs for children with congenital heart disease in the United States. Activities include fetal cardiology, transesophageal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance and cardiac computed tomography. The instructor (Advanced fellow) in non-invasive imaging will participate in our fellowship program as a non-ACGME fellow. This structure is in place to train this talented fellow while he/she participates in inpatient rounds and outpatient care.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
· Maintain timely and complete EPIC chart notes, reports, and communication with primary care/referring physicians and other relevant subspecialty physicians. Participate in multidisciplinary clinical management initiatives with other subsections within Pediatric Cardiology.
· Participate in division and department quality improvement initiatives.
· Maintain varied hours on a rotated schedule with other physicians to ensure that there is always a physician on-call during non-business hours.
· Attend patient rounds and complete consultation and inpatient notes. Comply with all billing, coding, documentation, and regulatory requirements.
· Participate in divisional conferences, Department of Pediatrics grand rounds, morbidity and mortality conferences, and faculty development education.
· Additional clinical responsibilities will include outpatient Cardiology coverage and inpatient service as well as conference preparation and on-call duties.
COMMITMENT OF DIVERSITY:
Columbia University is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and Educator. The University is dedicated to the goal of building a culturally diverse and pluralistic faculty and staff committed to teaching and working in a diverse environment, and strongly encourages applications from women, minorities, individuals with disabilities, and veterans.
Columbia University welcomes applications from individuals who may have had nontraditional career paths, or who may have taken time off for family reasons (e.g. children, caring for disabled or elderly family), or who have achieved excellence in careers outside of academia (e.g., in professional or industry service). The University is responsive to the needs of dual career couples and is committed to supporting the work-life balance of its faculty. We are interested in candidates who have a record of success advising and mentoring individuals from groups underrepresented in higher education and is particularly interested in candidates who have research interests in subjects that will contribute to the understanding of diversity and equal opportunity.

jobs.title: Open Rank Faculty Position in Clinical Psychology, Department of Psychology, Vanderbilt University
jobs.institution: Vanderbilt University: Psychology
jobs.description:
The Clinical Psychology Program in the Department of Psychology of the College of Arts & Science at Vanderbilt University invites applications for a faculty position in Clinical Psychology at any rank, tenure-track or tenured. The Vanderbilt Clinical Psychology Program is internationally recognized for its strength in experimental psychopathology, affective science, intervention research, and clinical neuroscience. The successful candidate will join the core faculty of our APA- and PCSAS-accredited clinical science training program, which is designed to prepare students for academic/research careers in clinical psychology.
The Department of Psychology, housed within the College of Arts and Science, is a community of 27 full-time faculty with a strong commitment to excellence in research and teaching in psychology and neuroscience. Our faculty are organized into three overlapping areas representing clinical science, cognition and cognitive neuroscience, and neuroscience. We have strong collaborative relations with the Department of Psychology and Human Development in Peabody College at Vanderbilt, hosting with them a joint PhD program in Psychological Sciences, and with the Department of Psychiatry and other departments affiliated with the Vanderbilt University Medical Center. For information about our faculty, department, and interdisciplinary opportunities, please see https://as.vanderbilt.edu/psychology/.
Vanderbilt University is a top ranked private research university. Its 330-acre park-like campus is located on the western edge of downtown Nashville, TN, known colloquially as Music City and is consistently rated as one of the best cities in the US in which to live and work.

jobs.title: Head of the Department of Biological Sciences
jobs.institution: Carnegie Mellon University: Biological Sciences
jobs.description:
The Department of Biological Sciences at Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) seeks an accomplished scientist and ambitious, collaborative leader to serve as its next head. The head will hold a newly endowed headship in Biological Sciences and will lead the department at a pivotal moment of opportunity, including overseeing the opening of expanded research space and new teaching laboratories in the Richard King Mellon Hall of Science, scheduled to open in early 2028. The candidate will articulate and execute a compelling vision for elevating the department’s scientific impact and external support. The head will advance the quality and visibility of life sciences research across the university, leveraging CMU’s highly collaborative environment and distinctive strengths in computational biology, engineering, computer science, and machine learning to build ambitious interdisciplinary research programs.
The Department of Biological Sciences is one of four departments in the Mellon College of Science. The college also plays a central role in the cross-university Neuroscience Institute, which has strong ties to Biological Sciences. Biological Sciences is home to 20 internationally recognized tenure-track faculty, with strengths in molecular and cellular biology, neuroscience, microbiology, and evolutionary and developmental biology. The tenure-track faculty include a dynamic group of assistant professors hired in the past five years who have already been successful in obtaining external funding. The department has an engaged and collegial community, including 60-70 graduate students, six staff members, postdoctoral fellows, and research scientists. The department also includes 16 teaching-track faculty located in Pittsburgh and at our Qatar campus. Faculty and staff are dedicated to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education, including a PhD program and specialized master’s programs, including Computational Biology and Quantitative Biology and Bioinformatics.
CMU and the department have a long and notable history of innovation and technology development. Faculty in the Department of Biological Sciences have developed new methods for biological imaging, microscopy, molecular visualization, and cell tracking. Currently, faculty in the department hold grants from the NIH, NSF, and multiple private Foundations. The scientific environment in Pittsburgh is vibrant and collaborative. Many faculty hold secondary appointments in other units both within CMU and at the University of Pittsburgh; collaboration through shared graduate students and externally funded research is common.
The successful candidate will have a record of significant scientific achievement and sustained success in securing external research funding. They will bring demonstrated leadership in building research programs, recruiting and developing outstanding faculty, strengthening graduate education, and fostering productive partnerships. They will have a passion for building on the department’s strengths and fostering an environment in which faculty, staff, and students can excel, thereby advancing the department’s ambitions and impact. They will advocate effectively for the department, cultivate philanthropic and institutional support, and position Biological Sciences for substantial growth in scientific excellence, impact, and national visibility.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor position in Analytical Chemistry
jobs.institution: Colby College: Department of Chemistry
jobs.description: The Department of Chemistry at Colby College invites applications for a tenure-track, Assistant Professor position in analytical chemistry to begin fall 2027. We welcome applications from analytical chemists in all disciplines with preference for expertise in environmental applications, particularly in aqueous or terrestrial settings. The Colby Chemistry Department offers excellent instrumentation and computational resources to support analytical work. The College has a vibrant program in environmental sciences bridging multiple departments and partnerships with regional institutions such as Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences, The Seven Lakes Alliance, and Colby’s Island Campus. For more information about this position, please see: https://web.colby.edu/analytical/. The position carries an average annual teaching load of 4.5 courses. The anticipated salary range for this position is $92,700 to $96,700, commensurate with rank, experience, qualifications, and other relevant factors. Research is supported with a competitive startup package. Application review will begin October 9, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Faculty Position- Department of Molecular Physiology and Biophysics, Vanderbilt Center for Addiction Research (VCAR)
jobs.institution: Vanderbilt University: Molecular Physiology & Biophysics
jobs.description:
The Department of Molecular Physiology and Biophysics (MPB) and the Vanderbilt Center for Addiction Research (VCAR) invite applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position from outstanding early-career investigators whose research focuses on areas fundamental to understanding substance use disorders.
We welcome applicants who are employing innovative experimental, computational, and translational approaches to investigate the molecular, cellular, circuit, systems, and behavioral mechanisms underlying substance use disorders and related biological processes. We seek candidates who are investigating fundamental mechanisms relevant to addiction, including—but not limited to—motivation and reward, reinforcement learning, decision-making, feeding and ingestive behavior, pain, stress and resilience, neural circuit function, synaptic plasticity, neuropharmacology, neuroimmune interactions, molecular signaling, and neuroendocrinology, and/or who are investigating topics relevant to addiction from the perspective of affective neuroscience, genetics and genomics, and/or computational and systems neuroscience.
The successful candidate will have a primary appointment in the Department of Molecular Physiology and Biophysics (MPB) on the investigator track and will be a member of the Vanderbilt Center for Addiction Research (VCAR).
VCAR is the intellectual hub for addiction research at Vanderbilt University: it brings together investigators across multiple schools and departments to elucidate the fundamental biology of substance use disorders. By fostering interdisciplinary collaborations among basic scientists, computational biologists, clinicians, and behavioral scientists, VCAR promotes innovative approaches to understanding the mechanisms of addiction, with the aim of developing new strategies for preventing and treating it. VCAR provides a dynamic scientific community with opportunities for collaboration, mentorship, trainee development, and shared research resources.
MPB is an exceptionally collaborative and intellectually vibrant environment with internationally recognized strengths in fields ranging from molecular physiology, neuroscience, and metabolism to structural biology, quantitative biology, and biomedical engineering.
The successful MPB/VCAR candidates will join a dynamic scientific community spanning the biological, biomedical, computational, engineering, and behavioral sciences. Vanderbilt offers state-of-the-art research facilities, outstanding shared resources, extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration across the School of Medicine Basic Sciences and the broader University, and a longstanding commitment to mentoring early-career investigators.
Applicants should demonstrate exceptional promise—more specifically, the capacity to establish an innovative, externally funded research program. The successful candidates will be expected to develop a rigorous independent research program, contribute to graduate and medical education, mentor trainees, and participate actively in the scientific community at Vanderbilt.
Applications will begin to be reviewed immediately, and the process will continue until the position is filled.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor of Urban Planning and Public Service
jobs.institution: New York University: Academic Affairs
jobs.description:
The NYU Wagner Graduate School of Public Service invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position in urban planning, with appointment to begin September 1, 2027. The position will be at the assistant professor level. Successful applicants will have a demonstrated record of research excellence and productivity, a promising research agenda, and a Ph.D. in a relevant field. We encourage more senior candidates to apply for our separate posting for an associate professor in urban planning.
NYU Wagner is a multidisciplinary school that prepares public service leaders to translate ideas into actions that have an effective and lasting impact on the public good. Wagner’s 35 full-time faculty members are trained in a wide variety of disciplines and share a commitment to addressing issues of public importance in their teaching, research and service. Wagner faculty members collaborate with other schools and departments across the university, including the Departments of Politics, Economics, and Sociology; School of Law; Stern School of Business; Tandon School of Engineering; and the College of Global Public Health. Wagner faculty members also have opportunities to collaborate with and hold leadership positions at various research centers like the NYU Furman Center, the Rudin Center, and the Marron Institute of Urban Management.
Successful candidates will teach in our urban planning program and demonstrate a research interest in cities, both globally and domestically. We welcome applications from scholars with interests in a wide range of urban topics, including infrastructure, housing, climate change, and technology, and who study these issues in different contexts. We are particularly interested in candidates who focus on the physical/spatial dimensions of cities, defined broadly, and those whose work focuses on pressing urban planning challenges more generally. We seek faculty candidates who are excited to teach a diverse population of students motivated to understand and improve urban communities.
In compliance with NYC's Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for the assistant professor position is $125,000-$145,000.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Clinical Psychology
jobs.institution: Vanderbilt University: Psychology and Human Development
jobs.description:
Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Clinical Psychology
Department of Psychology and Human Development
Peabody College of Education and Human Development
Vanderbilt University
The Department of Psychology and Human Development in Peabody College at Vanderbilt University invites applications for two tenure-track positions as Assistant Professor in Clinical Psychology. The Clinical Psychology Ph.D. program at Vanderbilt spans two departments (the Department of Psychology and the Department of Psychology and Human Development), subscribes to the clinical science training model, and is PCSAS- and APA-accredited. We seek exceptional clinical scientists with demonstrated records of methodologically rigorous and conceptually strong research, clear potential to secure extramural funding, and a commitment to effective teaching and mentoring.
We are particularly interested in clinical scientists who apply artificial intelligence (AI), computational, and/or advanced quantitative approaches to enhance the prediction, explanation, assessment, prevention, or treatment of psychopathology, particularly across development. Ideally, these scientists would foster collaborations with the College of Connected Computing. Applications could include using AI-related methods to enhance research methods, developing predictive models for risk and treatment response, and/or integrating AI into evidence-based interventions. Relevant approaches include those of AI’s subfields, such as machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, speech and behavioral signal processing, digital phenotyping, passive sensing, advanced quantitative and computational modeling, personalized and technology-enabled interventions, among other innovative methods.
Successful candidates will maintain active, externally funded research programs that apply innovative methods (e.g., quantitative, analytic, computational). We welcome applicants whose primary training is in clinical or developmental science with clinical applications. Responsibilities include leading an active, collaborative research program, teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels, research mentoring, and contributing to departmental, college, and university service.
Vanderbilt University is a top-ranked private research university located near downtown Nashville, TN, a vibrant and rapidly growing city known for its music, food, culture, and access to outdoor recreation. Peabody College is consistently ranked among the top schools of education in the U.S., and the joint clinical psychology program is currently ranked #9 by U.S. News & World Report. The Department of Psychology and Human Development is home to highly collaborative faculty with strengths in developmental science, cognitive psychology, clinical psychological science, and quantitative methods. We maintain close connections with the Department of Psychology in the College of Arts and Science, the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, and the Vanderbilt Kennedy Center. Vanderbilt has outstanding research infrastructure and opportunities for collaboration, including the Vanderbilt University Institute of Imaging Science, Vanderbilt Brain Institute, Data Science Institute, LIVE Learning Innovation Incubator, and Advanced Computing Center for Research and Education.

jobs.title: Faculty Positions in the Division of Addiction Medicine
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: Perelman School of Medicine - Family Medicine and Community Health
jobs.description:
The Division of Addiction Medicine within the Department of Family Medicine and Community Health at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for multiple faculty positions in Addiction Medicine in the non-tenure Academic Clinician (AC) track. Successful candidates will hold an M.D. or D.O. degree and must have primary board in a recognized ABMS or AOA Specialty and must be board certified in Addiction Medicine. They should have experience in hospital-based addiction medicine consultation and in underserved and vulnerable patient care and an interest in a career in academic medicine. Preferred candidates will have completion of an Addiction Medicine fellowship; experience in inpatient consultation services; experience caring for patients with opioid use disorder and other substance use disorders; experience working in Bridge/OTP or low-barrier treatment programs.
Teaching responsibilities may include participation in the education and supervision of residents, fellows, and medical students in inpatient, consultative, ambulatory, and Bridge/OTP settings. Opportunities for educational leadership and program development may be available for the right candidate.
Clinical responsibilities may include clinical care based primarily at Pennsylvania Hospital, Penn Presbyterian Medical Center, Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, HUP Cedar, Bridge/Opioid Treatment Services (OTP) services, and other Penn Medicine-affiliated clinical settings. Faculty may participate in ambulatory addiction medicine, Bridge/OTP services, treatment of opioid and other substance use disorders, hospital-based addiction treatment, community-based addiction services, resident and fellow supervision, and multidisciplinary care coordination. All faculty members will devote a portion of their clinical effort to inpatient Addiction Medicine consult services at one or more Penn Medicine hospitals, including Pennsylvania Hospital, Penn Presbyterian Medical Center, the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, and HUP Cedar.
The Division of Addiction Medicine is recruiting for three full-time faculty positions that will support Penn Medicine's growing addiction medicine clinical, educational, and community programs. These positions offer flexibility in clinical practice location and scope while supporting access to evidence-based addiction treatment across Penn Medicine.
The Division of Addiction Medicine serves diverse patients across Philadelphia, including many individuals and communities that have historically experienced barriers to health care access and health equity. We seek candidates who demonstrate a commitment to caring for medically and socially complex patient populations and who have experience working in underserved communities and resource-limited clinical settings.
Academic Clinician faculty are not required to maintain an independent research program; however, scholarly activity, quality improvement, curriculum development, and educational innovation are encouraged and supported.

jobs.title: Instructor - Health Care Sciences [Req#: 976105, Position#: 133907]
jobs.institution: UT Southwestern: 250002 - Health Care Sciences Admin
jobs.description:
Works under minimal supervision to provide project management support to strategic initiatives within a department under the direction of department leadership.
This position helps support the School of Health Professions by coordinating academic and research-related initiatives that enhance faculty development, student learning, and program quality. It is ideal for a PhD-trained professional with experience in clinical and educational research, particularly in qualitative and mixed-methods analysis. Position will also assist in the implementation of institutional and federal standards, foster compliance through data-informed practices, and contribute to strategic planning and program evaluation.

jobs.title: Associate Research Scientist - Magnetically Confined Plasma Research
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Applied Physics and Applied Mathematics
jobs.description:
The Department of Applied Physics and Applied Mathematics (APAM) at Columbia University in the City of New York invites applications for Associate Research Scientist positions in the area of magnetically confined plasma research. There are up to 3 positions under consideration.
The successful candidate will advance research in magnetically confined plasmas and support the broader goals of the Columbia Fusion Research Center. In the tokamak area, the candidate may conduct research on experimental tokamak facilities in the public sector. Examples include the DIII-D tokamak located at General Atomics or the National Spherical Torus Experiment Upgrade located at Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory, or tokamaks located abroad. In the stellarator area, the candidate may conduct research in coil optimization, energetic particle physics, and other related activities. Activities may also be conducted in support of industrially sponsored research contracts originating from a wide array of sponsors, including concepts beyond tokamaks and stellarators. The successful candidate will also be expected to assist in the mentorship of more junior scientists, post-doctoral researchers, and students. In addition, the candidate is expected to conduct both supporting and independent research towards the execution of the Columbia Fusion Research Center research program, likely supporting multiple research awards.
Candidates for professional officer of research positions are expected to have established their ability to conduct original, independent scientist research. To the rank of an associate research scientist, candidate’s qualifications and contributions to their fields of research must be equivalent to those of an assistant professor. All candidates for all officer of research positions are expected to be able to work well in a team and to communicate effectively the results of their research or research activities both orally and in writing.
The level of appointment is commensurate with experience. The earliest position is expected to begin on approximately Jan 1st 2027 or sooner if possible, with possible additional positions being filled later in 2027.
Minimum Qualifications: Ph.D. (or equivalent professional degree) in plasma physics or a related field, and experience with different computer environments and languages especially Python, Matlab, IDL, FORTRAN and UNIX/LINX.
Preferred Qualifications: Familiarity of working with magnetically confined plasma computational modeling tools and their application to interpret experimental data. Familiarity with magnetically confined plasma experimental data and measurement methods. Demonstrated track record of mentorship of junior scientists, post-doctoral fellows, or students. Publications in top-rated journals in the field and presentations at national and international conferences
Candidates should be open to relocation to the New York City area.

jobs.title: Visiting Assistant Professor in Art (Photography)
jobs.institution: Hamilton College: Hamilton College Faculty
jobs.description:
The Art Department at Hamilton College invites applications for a Visiting Assistant Professor with expertise in photography whose work is grounded in studio practice, scholarship and teaching. The successful candidate’s research and teaching will situate photographic practices within historical, cultural, and interdisciplinary frameworks. This is a temporary one-year position for the 2027-2028 academic year. Teaching expectation is three courses in the fall and two courses in the spring, with additional responsibility for mentoring senior photo concentrators and overseeing Hamilton’s analog darkroom. The successful candidate can expect active support for their creative work. We are seeking candidates who can demonstrate their experience in teaching or working with broadly diverse student populations while contributing to a vibrant learning community that values academic freedom, creativity, and intellectual curiosity. Your cover letter should address the ways in which you would enhance the educational experience of students and further the College’s educational goals.
This position requires a strong grounding in traditional photographic processes and materials including analog film-based and wet darkroom processes, large format photography, and color digital photographic production. The successful candidate will have the ability to teach a strong foundation in perceptual, formal, and critical skills within a liberal arts context and to engage students in the social and theoretical dimensions of contemporary photographic practice. Additional experience in other media and types of practice is also welcome. We seek candidates who possess a capacity to interweave theory and practice, who demonstrate effective collaborative skills, and who display a commitment to undergraduate education in the liberal arts.
The Art department at Hamilton College is a vibrant and robust department of six full-time faculty serving 15-20 concentrators per year, as well as hundreds of non-major students each year. We are fortunate to teach in a state-of-the-art building that was completed in 2014 and which supports both analog practices as well as emerging technologies across 2D, 3D and time-based media offerings. Additional information about our program can be found at https://academics.hamilton.edu/art/list-art-studios.
Candidates must have an MFA, a record of effective teaching in higher education, and a demonstrated record of scholarly and creative achievement. The expected 9-month salary range for this position is $80,000 to $82,500. Applicants should submit a cover letter stating their motivation for teaching at a small, liberal arts college as well as their vision for the role of photography in a visual art program, curriculum vitae, up to 20 images of their own creative work (with captions), up to 20 images of student work (with captions), syllabi for an introductory and advanced level course in photography, and the names and contact information for three references who have agreed to provide letters of recommendation upon request. Letters will only be requested of finalists. Materials should be addressed to Robert Knight, Search Committee Chair via Interfolio at https://apply.interfolio.com/194067. Please contact help@interfolio.com if you have questions or problems with your uploads. Questions regarding the search may be directed to Robert Knight at rbknight@hamilton.edu. Applications will begin to be considered on January 15, 2027 and the position will remain open until filled.
For additional information about our current programs, please visit our Department and Digital Arts Program websites at:
https://www.hamilton.edu/academics/departments/Home?dept=Art
https://www.hamilton.edu/academics/departments/Home?dept=Digital%20Arts
Hamilton College is a residential liberal arts college located in central New York. The College has built its reputation on the teaching excellence and leading scholarship of its faculty, and on the academic distinction and intellectual curiosity of its approximately 2000 students who take advantage of Hamilton’s open curriculum (https://www.hamilton.edu/academics/open-curriculum). Accomplished faculty, highly capable and motivated students, and a student-faculty ratio of 9:1 provide an educational experience that emphasizes academic excellence, intellectual and cultural diversity, and respect for differences in the development of students as engaged members of their communities. Hamilton’s commitment to diversity is embodied in its need-blind admission policy for US Citizens and Permanent Residents; furthermore, Hamilton College meets the full demonstrated financial need for all admitted and enrolled students during their four years on campus. Please visit the college website for more information (www.hamilton.edu).
Hamilton College is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating an accessible, supportive environment and an educational experience that recognizes a wide array of experiences, backgrounds and viewpoints as integral components of academic excellence. Candidates who can contribute to those goals are encouraged to apply and discuss their strengths in these areas. Applicants with dual-career considerations can find other Hamilton and nearby academic job listings at https://www.hercjobs.org/regions/higher-ed-careers-upstate-new-york/, as well as additional information at https://www.hamilton.edu/dof/faculty-development/resources-for-prospective-or-new-faculty/opportunities-for-spouses-or-partners (Opportunities for Spouses or Partners). Hamilton provides domestic partner benefits.

jobs.title: Head of Scholarly Communications
jobs.institution: The University of Chicago: The Library
jobs.description:
The Head of Scholarly Communications shapes how the University of Chicago shares, preserves, and elevates its research. They will guide a growing portfolio of open scholarship and repository services, lead strategy in a rapidly shifting publishing environment, and serve as a campus-wide voice for sustainable, equitable scholarly communication.
This position reports to the Director of Digital Scholarship and works closely with colleagues across the Library and the university. The ideal candidate will bring expertise in open scholarship, copyright, persistent identifiers, and compliance with funder mandates. They will also oversee the institutional repository, UChicago Knowledge, and provide leadership for the staff who run it day to day.
Responsibilities:
Partner with the Director to set direction for scholarly communication services, ensuring they’re forward-looking, realistic, and aligned with broader Library priorities.
Design and deliver inclusive, sustainable services that support open scholarship, long-term preservation, research information management needs, and wide dissemination of University research outputs.
Supervise and mentor the Repository Services Manager. Guide policy, development, and operations for UChicago Knowledge.
Work directly with faculty, students, and staff to help them manage and share their work, including copyright, PIDs, funder requirements, and more.
Provide copyright and scholarly communication expertise across the Library. Collaborate with librarians to create strong outreach, training, and campus engagement.
Partner with campus IT and research computing units to evaluate, pilot, and implement technologies that strengthen scholarly communication infrastructure.
Participate in national conversations on standards, best practices, and research lifecycle management.
Play an active role in Library committees, strategic initiatives, and diversity efforts.
Perform other duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Professor of British/Anglophone Literature - Open Rank
jobs.institution: Occidental College: English
jobs.description:
The Department of English at Occidental College invites applications for a tenure‐track Open Rank, Professor of British/Anglophone Literature with appointment to begin August 2027.
The English Department is searching for a new colleague in British/Anglophone Literature. The specialization is open, though the department is especially interested in the fields of Long Eighteenth Century, the History of the Novel, Romanticism, British Modernism, Contemporary Global Anglophone literature. We welcome a range of methodologies that practice close reading, examine literary form, and attend to literary history. The new hire will offer courses in Modern British Literature, from its 18th-century origins to its 21st-century manifestations. This will include ENGL 288: Modern British Traditions, as well as other courses at the 100, 200, and 300 levels in their area(s) of specialization. In addition, the new hire will teach required seminar courses that rotate among members of the department, including ENGL 290: Literary Methods, the ENGL 390: Junior Seminar and ENGL 490: Senior Seminar. We are particularly interested in courses that would meet College Core requirements or would engage with the city and communities of Los Angeles. As necessary, the new hire will contribute to the First Year Seminar program, which focuses on writing and community-engagement. The new hire will also have the opportunity to mentor undergraduate researchers in Oxy’s renowned Summer Undergraduate Research Program. The new hire will have an active research agenda, producing scholarship that is commensurate with their rank. Finally, the new hire will participate in the life and development of the department, advise students, and serve on broader college-wide committees.
The Department of English studies literature to develop our critical and creative potential in a nation and world going through drastic changes. We embrace the view that historically, geographically, and culturally grounded readings of literature deepen its aesthetic value. Literature continues to be a wellspring for other creative mediums (including television, film, music, visual art, performance art, and beyond). We also introduce our students to archival research in Occidental’s special collections as well as other libraries and archives in Southern California.
Our students embrace literature’s role in nourishing their critical and creative potential. Every English major researches and writes their own critical analysis of a literary work in their Senior Comprehensive Project. In recent years, students have taken up a range of topics for their Senior Comprehensive, including Gothic fiction,Margaret Atwood’s fiction, Toni Morrison’s fiction, Ecoliterature, Ekphrastic Poetry, Anticolonial Literature, Fantasy Novels, the relationship between Literature and Gaming, and Reginald Shepherd’s Elegies. Our students who take on the creative writing emphasis have completed poetry chapbooks, children’s literature, and short fiction. English majors and minors comprise the majority of the editorial collective that publishes The Oz, Occidental’s literary magazine that features short fiction, poetry, experimental writing, and visual art from students across campus. Our students have also made their mark across Los Angeles, from interning with the Los Angeles Review of Books to volunteering in mutual aid projects. Our graduates go on to work in independent publishing, education, marketing, and law, among other fields. Our faculty are committed teacher-scholars who bring critical inquiry and discovery into the classroom. They establish themselves as exceptional researchers and practitioners in their fields and they provide departmental and college-wide service, as well as service to their professions. As a small institution with a commitment to Shared Governance, faculty across the College collaborate in maintaining the excellence of the College’ academic program.
Located within the vibrant city of Los Angeles, Occidental is committed to a community-engaged curriculum—faculty build fieldwork, visits to local museums and cultural organizations, and long-standing partnerships into their courses. Occidental is also committed to undergraduate research, regularly mentoring students in Occidental’s hallmark summer research program. For decades, Occidental has been a leader in creating access for a diverse student body. That diversity enriches the education of all students. We seek an innovative teacher, scholar, mentor, and colleague who wishes to work in such an environment and who shares the commitments articulated in the mission of the College.

jobs.title: Student Reception & Package Desk Assistant
jobs.institution: Case Western Reserve University: Case School of Engineering (STUDENT)
jobs.description:
Position Summary
The Student Reception & Package Desk Assistant serves as the first point of contact for students, faculty, staff, and visitors. This position is responsible for providing excellent customer service at the reception desk, managing package distribution and tracking, answering questions, and supporting daily administrative operations. The ideal candidate is dependable, organized, professional, and committed to creating a welcoming environment.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Reception & Customer Service
Greet students, staff, faculty, and visitors in a friendly and professional manner.
Answer and direct phone calls, emails, and in-person inquiries.
Provide accurate information regarding office services, programs, and campus resources.
Maintain a clean, organized, and welcoming reception area.
Monitor office traffic and assist visitors with locating appropriate resources or personnel.
Package Management
Receive, log, organize, and distribute incoming packages and mail.
Verify recipient identification before package release.
Maintain accurate package tracking records using designated software and procedures.
Notify recipients of package arrivals in a timely manner.
Assist with inventory management and storage organization.
Report package discrepancies, lost items, or delivery issues to the supervisor.
Administrative Support
Perform basic clerical tasks such as filing, scanning, data entry, and document preparation.
Assist with departmental projects and events as assigned.
Maintain confidentiality of student and university information.
Support office operations by completing additional duties as needed.

jobs.title: COMM 375 – International Business and the Nonmarket Environment
jobs.institution: Smith School of Business at Queen's University
jobs.description:
A term adjunct position is open at the Smith School of Business for an instructor to teach at our main campus in a lecture-style undergraduate course in the Commerce program. The position is to teach International Business and the Nonmarket Environment – Comm 375 in the winter term. Teaching Comm 375 will generally include teaching twenty-four “one-and-a-half hour” sessions from January to April 2027. The successful applicant will be required to teach 100% of one section of COMM 375 with a maximum enrollment of 55 students.
The course is described as follows:
This course introduces students to the relevant non-market actors that affect the international business environment and provides a broad range of theoretical frameworks for understanding and shaping their motivations, capabilities and strategies. Topics will include the international trading environment, political and country risk analysis, the motivations of national governments, international and national regulators, and the interaction of firms with government, industry and lobby groups. In covering a wide range of topics, this course favors breadth over depth. The course primarily draws on readings from lecture notes, classroom discussion and debate.
The open section for COMM 375 has been scheduled in the Winter term as follows:
Section 001 – Tuesdays 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM / Thursdays 08:30 AM to 10:00 AM
Compensation
The salary for a term adjunct teaching one section of a course in our Commerce program is $13,856 (excluding vacation pay). This salary is pro-rated based on course credit.

jobs.title: Student Assistant, Office of Government Relations
jobs.institution: Case Western Reserve University: UGEN (STUDENT)
jobs.description:
Duration: 2026-2027 academic year
Pay Rate: $15/hour
Schedule: part-time, flexible daytime/weekday hours
About Us
Case Western Reserve University's Office of Government Relations serves as the university's point of contact for interaction with federal and state government officials. The office monitors and responds to legislative and regulatory issues that impact the university, our students, and our research enterprise. The office serves as a campus-wide resource for protocols related to interactions with public officials.
Purpose and Scope
The Office of Government Relations seeks an organized, detail-oriented undergraduate student to provide administrative support to both the Associate Vice President and the Director of Government Relations. This Student Assistant position offers a unique experience to gain insights into higher education policy and government relations activities for a leading research university.
Key Responsibilities
Provide general office support, including organization, data entry, and document preparation.
Draft correspondence, briefing papers, agendas, itineraries, and other written materials and analysis.
Assist in tracking legislation and regulatory issues of importance to the university.
Watch, take notes, and report on congressional and state legislative hearings and other meetings of importance to the office and the university.
Provide logistical support for campus visits by elected officials, their staff, and other meetings of importance hosted by the office.

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor in Environmental Studies
jobs.institution: Tufts University: Environmental Studies
jobs.description:
The Environmental Studies Program at Tufts University (Medford, MA) invites applications for a full-time, non-tenure-track Assistant Teaching Professor in Environmental Studies, beginning September 1, 2027. This is a nine-month academic appointment paid over 12 months, with an initial two-year contract and the possibility of renewal thereafter.
We seek an innovative, interdisciplinary, and applied scholar in the social sciences who is committed to excellence in undergraduate teaching and mentorship, outreach, and collaboration. We welcome candidates with diverse academic backgrounds and expertise relevant to Environmental Studies, with particular interest in candidates who can contribute to the curriculum in the Sustainability, Policy, and Equity and Environmental Communication tracks of the Environmental Studies major. We are especially interested in candidates with a demonstrated record of interdisciplinary collaboration who can create meaningful opportunities for students to engage directly with practitioners, organizations, institutions, and communities. Candidates should be passionate about connecting classroom learning with real-world environmental challenges and professional pathways.
The successful candidate will contribute to the educational mission of the program through undergraduate teaching, advising, mentoring, and departmental and university-wide service. The position carries a teaching load of up to six courses per academic year, with a teaching load equivalent to four courses in the first year and five courses in the second year. Teaching responsibilities may include the program’s interdisciplinary gateway course, Introduction to Environmental Studies. Additional teaching may include an environmental communication course, research methods, advanced seminars and supervision of independent studies or theses. Experiential or community-based learning courses are highly valued. We seek a colleague who will be an engaged member of a vibrant, interdisciplinary community and who is eager to contribute to student engagement and community building within and outside of Tufts.
The Environmental Studies Program, established in 1984, is one of the oldest environmental undergraduate programs in the country. Student interest in the program continues to increase and is now one of the largest academic programs at Tufts University. The Environmental Studies Program prepares students to have a deep understanding of the critical issues facing society, essential analytical skills, and the ability to communicate their knowledge to their peers and the general public. We offer two majors and two minors and sponsor a wide range of extracurricular activities, including a weekly lecture series. More information about the program can be found at Go.tufts.edu/ENVS.

This arrangement allows for a dedicated focus on research while benefiting from mentorship and support from two senior faculty members.
A Ph.D. in philosophy or a closely related field is required prior to appointment. Candidates must show strong promise of excellence in both teaching and research. Applicants should provide the following:

jobs.title: Faculty Position in International Economics, Open Rank
jobs.institution: Georgetown University: Georgetown University in Qatar
jobs.description:
Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q) invites applications for one (1) open-rank core faculty position in International Economics.
We welcome applications from candidates in all fields of economics, with a preference for candidates conducting applied and empirically relevant research. This may include, but is not limited to, fields such as international economics, development economics, behavioral economics, labor economics, political economy, and applied microeconomics and macroeconomics. Applicants should demonstrate a strong research profile, evidenced by a substantial record of high-quality research accomplishments or, for more junior candidates, clear evidence of the potential to develop such a record. Candidates should also have an ambitious and active research agenda and a strong record of teaching excellence.
Appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, depending on the candidate’s experience and qualifications.
Qualifications
A Ph.D. in Economics.
A strong and active research agenda, with a demonstrated record of publication in leading economics journals or, for junior candidates, clear evidence of the potential to establish such a record.
A strong commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring, demonstrated through previous teaching experience and, for senior candidates, a sustained record of teaching effectiveness and student mentorship.
Academic Environment and Faculty Support
GU-Q offers a rich academic setting supported by strong institutional resources to enable excellence in teaching and research. Faculty typically teach two courses (or 6 credit hours) per semester (a 2-2 load), supported by best-in-class instructional infrastructure. This includes the Global Classroom, which connects students in Doha with peers in Washington, D.C., for live, cross-campus engagement, and access to collaborative research centers such as the Center for International and Regional Studies (CIRS).
To advance faculty scholarship and professional development, GU-Q provides:
Access to GU-Q faculty research funds.
Eligibility for funding through the Qatar Research, Development, and Innovation Council (QRDI).
Eligibility to apply for a summer research supplement equivalent to 2/9 of base salary.
Generous conference travel funding and professional development resources.
Compensation and Benefits
GU-Q offers a highly competitive compensation package by U.S. academic standards, along with an exceptional expatriate benefits package that includes:
Fully furnished, high-quality housing.
Transportation allowance.
Annual family home leave.
Worldwide health insurance coverage.
Private school tuition support for accompanying children.
Additional relocation and onboarding assistance.
About Georgetown University in Qatar
GU-Q was established in 2005 alongside other elite international universities in Education City, in partnership with Qatar Foundation. GU-Q is an integral part of Georgetown University, delivering the renowned School of Foreign Service’s Bachelor of Science in Foreign Service (BSFS) degree. Ranked first in the world in international relations by Foreign Policy magazine, this liberal arts program offers majors in International Politics, International History, Culture and Politics, International Economics, and Science, Technology, and International Affairs. The degree is awarded by Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. GU-Q is a research-focused, student-oriented institution with a globally competitive research and publications record. GU-Q values interdisciplinarity, and its faculty and students benefit from the opportunities offered by the wider academic ecosystem of Education City. For more information on GU-Q, see https://www.qatar.georgetown.edu.
Life in Qatar
Qatar offers a diverse, family-friendly living environment, with the cultural, educational, and recreational resources of a major global city. Public parks, beaches, sports facilities (including Education City’s extensive sports venues), museums, cafes, and restaurants abound, and a state-of-the-art metro system connects all parts of Doha and nearby locations. Within Education City, the iconic Qatar National Library, designed by Rem Koolhaas, provides free membership to faculty and students. Faculty at GU-Q also benefit from a close-knit Georgetown community, strong institutional support, and regular coordination between Doha and Washington, D.C. While the early months of 2026 brought instability to the region, Doha remains one of the safest cities in the world, and Qatar continues to rank highly in the Global Peace Index. Doha is connected by direct flights to more than 160 destinations in 90 countries. This short video offers a glimpse of what it is like to teach and live in Qatar.
Application Process
Review of applications will begin on October 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Applicants should provide a cover letter detailing teaching and research interests, curriculum vitae, the names and contact details of three scholarly references, and, if available, evidence of teaching excellence (such as recent student course ratings, peer observation reports, etc.).
All application materials must be submitted via Georgetown’s online application management system at https://apply.interfolio.com/194081.
Questions about the online application system should be directed to Ms. Carina Lawson at cl978@georgetown.edu. Queries about the position should be directed to Professor Ramon Cobo Reyes Cano at rc1557@georgetown.edu. Please reference “International Economics” in the subject line.

The position will be at the associate professor level. Successful applicants will have a demonstrated record of research excellence and productivity, a promising research agenda, and a Ph.D. in a relevant field. NYU Wagner is a multidisciplinary school that prepares public service leaders to translate ideas into actions that have an effective and lasting impact on the public good. Wagner’s 35 full-time faculty members are trained in a wide variety of disciplines and share a commitment to addressing issues of public importance in their teaching, research and service. Wagner faculty members collaborate with other schools and departments across the university, including the Departments of Politics, Economics, and Sociology; School of Law; Stern School of Business; Tandon School of Engineering; and the College of Global Public Health. Wagner faculty members also have opportunities to collaborate with and hold leadership positions at various research centers like the NYU Furman Center, the Rudin Center, and the Marron Institute of Urban Management.
Successful candidates will teach in our urban planning program and demonstrate a research interest in cities, both globally and domestically. We welcome applications from scholars with interests in a wide range of urban topics, including infrastructure, housing, climate change, and technology, and who study these issues in different contexts. We are particularly interested in candidates who focus on the physical/spatial dimensions of cities, defined broadly, and those whose work focuses on pressing urban planning challenges more generally. We seek faculty candidates who are excited to teach a diverse population of students motivated to understand and improve urban communities.

Arizona State University and The Biodesign Center for Personalized Diagnostics at the Biodesign Institute are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Scholar with expertise in cancer immunology and cancer biology. This role will lead pivotal initiatives in immunotherapeutic platform development and target discovery to advance precision oncology strategies.
Our center is engineering multiplexed single-cell assays to screen and identify patient-specific immunogenic neoantigens and their corresponding immune receptors for direct translation into therapeutic agents. Concurrently, we integrate cutting-edge multi-omics, functional screening platforms, tumor-on-chip models, and patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models to uncover actionable mechanisms driving tumor-intrinsic signaling and immune/stromal microenvironment interactions. The successful candidate will serve as a scientific and operational leader across both research tracks, driving project execution, technology innovation, and team mentorship. We anticipate filling this role in October 2026.
Essential Duties:
Immunoproteomics & Assay Engineering: Lead the conceptualization, development, and optimization of high-throughput immunoproteomics and single-cell assay platforms.
Target Discovery & Validation: Identify and validate novel immunotherapeutic targets and small-molecule vulnerabilities using integrated multi-omics, primary organoid cultures, tumor-on-chip systems, and in vivo mouse models.
Research Dissemination: Lead manuscript development, contribute to grant applications and technical reports, and present research findings at scientific conferences.
Leadership & Mentorship: Oversee daily experimental workflows, train junior scientists and scientific trainees, and foster a collaborative laboratory environment.
Travel: Participate in occasional travel to scientific conferences and other research-related events, as needed.
Perform other duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Part-time lecturer for "Health Policy in a Global World"
jobs.institution: New York University: NYU Buenos Aires
jobs.description:
NYU Buenos Aires is currently recruiting for a part-time lecturer to teach "Health Policy in a Global World" sponsored by NYU's School of Global Public Health. Teaching begins in the Spring 2027 semester (Jan 21st - May 5th 2027).
Course format
The course is taught in English and meets for 3 hours per week, for 14 instructional weeks plus the final examination week, and office hours. The instructor role includes all preparations, delivery of lecture materials in an interactive manner, providing feedback on assignments and all grading in a timely manner.
Course Description
This course introduces students to key concepts in health policy formation, implementation and evaluation in a global context. Using a comparative lens, students explore organization, financing and delivery of health care services and health systems around the world and examine the role of governmental, private, and non-profit agencies in delivering health care and other services. The course is multidisciplinary, employing public policy, sociological, political science, economic, and ethical perspectives. The overall goal is to build an understanding of the fundamental ideas, issues, and problems currently debated in global health policy and management and to provide a foundation for future studies and careers in the global health field.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Public Management

jobs.description:
The McCourt School of Public Policy at Georgetown University invites applications for a tenure line Assistant Professor position in Public Management. We are a rapidly growing policy school in the heart of Washington DC, which includes a diverse mix of scholars from economics, political science, sociology, public administration, and other domains. We seek a scholar who will contribute to, and thrive in, our vibrant inter-disciplinary research community.
We are looking for candidates with a career trajectory for a high level of academic success in public management, including presenting at and publishing in respected public management, public administration and policy implementation outlets. We will consider outstanding candidates with any area of research focus in the functioning of public services and implementation of policy. Expertise in the following areas is welcomed but not required: environment and sustainability, social policy and inequality, immigration and migration, or artificial intelligence.
We offer an undergraduate program and a variety of graduate programs. Successful candidates are expected to teach in both programs, specifically comparative public management, public management, as well as other elective courses in their own areas of research interest.
Applicants should have a PhD in public management, public administration, public affairs, political science, public policy or a related field. Candidates for a position at the Assistant Professor rank must have completed or expect to complete their Ph.D. by the start date of August 1, 2027.
Materials should be submitted online to Interfolio. The Committee will begin reviewing applications on October 16, 2026.
Required Application Materials:
Cover Letter (including research themes, teaching approach and accomplishments)
Curriculum Vita
Writing Sample (e.g., dissertation chapter, job market paper, or lead-author publication)
Contact Information of three References (reference letters will be solicited at a later stage)
The projected salary for this position is $101,165-$115,000, which represents the full range of anticipated compensation for this position. jobs.title: Assistant, Associate, Full Professor (Tenured/Tenure-Track) in Computer Science
jobs.institution: The University of Texas at Austin: Department of Computer Science
jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science at The University of Texas at Austin invites applications for tenure-track faculty positions. We are accepting applications from outstanding candidates in all areas of computer science.
In addition to all core areas within CS, we encourage candidates with strong technical grounding in computer science whose work creates opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, including potential partial or joint appointments in other departments at The University of Texas at Austin. As part of UT Austin’s School of Computing, Computer Science has close ties with the Department of Statistics and Data Sciences and the Department of Information, creating additional opportunities for joint appointments and cross-disciplinary research. We are also particularly interested in candidates advancing AI for Science, as well as those working specifically at the intersection of computer science with neuroscience, biology, or medicine.
All interdisciplinary candidates are encouraged to send applications to all relevant departments for better university-wide coordination. Candidates working at the intersection of CS and Neuroscience are particularly encouraged to send applications to both departments to facilitate an explicit joint search. Candidates may also apply to the Neuroscience position via Interfolio (apply.interfolio.com/193043).
All positions are subject to the availability of funding.
The department is ranked among the top computer science departments in the country. It has 64 tenured and tenure-track faculty members across all areas of computer science. Beginning in Fall 2026, Computer Science will be one of three founding academic units in UT Austin’s new School of Computing, alongside Statistics and Data Science and Information. The new School is designed to strengthen collaboration and create new opportunities for cross-departmental research and education. Many faculty also participate in interdisciplinary programs and centers across the University, including Texas Robotics, the Machine Learning Laboratory, the Institute on Foundations of Machine Learning (an NSF AI Institute), Learning Directed Operating Systems (NSF Expeditions in Computing), the Center for Generative AI, the Good Systems Grand Challenge on Ethical AI, the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC), and the Oden Institute for Computational Engineering and Science.
Austin, the capital of Texas, is a major technology hub, home to significant operations from companies such as such as Amazon, AMD, Apple, Applied Materials, AT&T, Dell, Google, IBM, Meta, NVIDIA, Samsung, Silicon Labs, and Tesla. For more information about the department, please visit https://cs.utexas.edu.

Wang lab studies 1) oxidative stress / mitochondrial dysfunction-induced neurodegeneration and neuronal cell death in aging-related neurological diseases (Wang Y et al., Science, 2016; Liu S et al., Molecular Neurodegeneration, 2021; Zhou M et al., Nature Communications, 2025) and 2) role of PARPs and PARP-1-dependent cell death (PARthanatos) regulators in health and diseases (Yang M et al., NAR 2022; Wang Y et al., Nature Communications 2021; Ruan Z et al., Cell Mol Life Sci 2021; Wang Y et al., Molecular Psychiartry, 2022). Our goal is to understand neurodegeneration and cell death induced by brain injury, mitochondrial dysfunction and/or aging-related genome instability. jobs.title: Associate Research Scientist
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Taub Institute
jobs.description:
The Taub Institute for Research on Alzheimer's Disease and the Aging Brian is seeking a talented and highly motivated scientist with strong expertise in biochemistry, molecular and cellular biology for the position of an Associate Research Scientist. The position will involve participation in NIH-funded projects aimed at understanding the mechanisms of neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental diseases. The projects employ multidisciplinary approaches in the areas of genomics, RNA/protein biochemistry and neuroscience using cellular and animal model systems.
We are primarily interested in candidates with wet-lab experience in animal models and microglia primary cultures. The core focus areas are innate immunity, tau and amyloid pathology, single- cell/single-nucleus transcriptomics, proteomics. The candidate in this position will have to utilize various in vivo and in vitro techniques to investigate the relationship between synaptic tau, proteolysis in immune cells and pathways related to memory and plasticity. The applicant will carry out experimental work on research projects established in liaison with the PI and to be performed either independently or in collaboration with postdoctoral research scientists and graduate students.
