jobs.title: Associate Research Scientist, part-time non-exempt
jobs.institution: New York University: Anthropology Department
jobs.description:
Associate Research Scientist (Area: sensory aging)
A part-time non-exempt Associate Research Scientist will support research and data generation related to sensory aging and function across the lifespan, using multi-omic measures to understand how social, environmental, and life-history factors shape sensory phenotypes. The Associate Research Scientist will work with Prof. James Higham, and in close collaboration with Prof. Amanda Melin, University of Calgary. The Associate Research Scientist will access and analyse samples in CBRU’s long-term biobank, with particular emphasis on organizing, preparing, and shipping samples for multi-omic data generation. Together, these approaches provide an opportunity to investigate how individuals’ sensory systems differ in molecular composition and putative function and health with age, and how these differences are shaped by their social and ecological environments. The position offers opportunities to collaborate on multiple ongoing and planned research studies, develop experience in new methods and techniques, and contribute to dissemination of findings through publications and conferences. The Associate Research Scientist will spend time at NYU and UCalgary for training, sample processing and analyses. The position is available immediately. The position is available for up to 500 hours, for approximately 12 months.
Key Responsibilities
- Oversee the processing of biological sample (tissues, excreta and body fluids) data.
- Work with PIs to organize timelines and processing priorities.
- Establish standard operating protocols for processing.
- Organize shipping of samples to core facilities for data generation, and storage and transfer of large data files.
- Contribute to initial quality assessments and analyses of received data
- Contribute to the preparation of grant applications and peer-reviewed manuscripts.
This position is based in New York and the selected candidate will be expected to work onsite as of their effective start date.
We welcome applications from international candidates; however, please note that NYU is not an E-Verify employer and therefore unable to support STEM OPT extensions.
In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $28-$32 per hour. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) the specific grant funding and the terms of the research grant when extending an offer.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, tenure-track
jobs.institution: The University of Texas at Austin: Department of Molecular Biosciences
jobs.description:
The Department of Molecular Biosciences at the University of Texas at Austin invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level in the field of biochemistry, with an emphasis on metabolism. We are particularly interested in collaborative and interdisciplinary scientists passionate about pursuing a mechanistic understanding of intermediary metabolism and metabolic regulation, elucidating connections with core biological processes or metabolic dysfunction, and developing innovative approaches to study cell metabolism. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, cellular and organellar metabolism, metabolic signaling, systems and computational approaches to metabolism, enzymology and metabolic regulation, structural and chemical biology of metabolic pathways, and the biochemical underpinnings of metabolic diseases (e.g., diabetes, obesity, tumor metabolism, and inborn errors of metabolism).
The Department of Molecular Biosciences is composed of a broad faculty whose research interests span many disciplines including biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology and biophysics, cell and developmental biology, plant biology, microbiology, immunology and infectious diseases, biotechnology, and systems and synthetic biology. We are excited to welcome collaborative scientists who actively interact with our faculty members and take advantage of our state-of-the-art facilities (see below).
Successful candidates are expected to establish and sustain a vibrant research program; serve as dedicated teachers and mentors at both the undergraduate and graduate levels; and assist in the administrative and governance functions of the department, the university, and the profession via service on committees as appropriate. Applicants at the assistant professor level must have plans to develop an exciting independent research program and a strong commitment to graduate and undergraduate education.
“What starts here changes the world.” UT Austin offers numerous resources and an exciting and interactive environment to foster creative interdisciplinary research. In addition to their research activities, our faculty are committed to the development of state-of-the art courses and real-world training experiences for undergraduate and graduate students as part of our core educational mission. Successful candidates will be eligible for membership in the Interdisciplinary Life Sciences Graduate Programs, which includes the Biochemistry Graduate Program, and collectively recruit a talented pool of graduate students each year. We also have outstanding core facilities, including those within the Center for Biomedical Research Support, the Texas Advanced Computing Center, and the Sauer Center for Structural Biology. The department has strong ties to other research units at UT Austin, including the School of Engineering, School of Pharmacy, Department of Computer Science, Oden Institute for Computational Engineering & Sciences, and Dell Medical School. This position offers excellent start-up funds, salary, and laboratory space in a dynamic and highly interactive research environment in the vibrant city of Austin. Applicants will also be encouraged to apply for support from the Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas (CPRIT).

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Curriculum and Instruction with a Specialization in Learning Technologies
jobs.institution: The University of Texas at Austin: Department of Curriculum & Instruction
jobs.description:
The Department of Curriculum and Instruction in the College of Education at The University of Texas at Austin seeks a faculty member at the assistant professor (tenure-track) level whose scholarship advances Learning Technologies in the areas of EC–12 education and teacher education.
We seek a scholar whose research examines the applications, policies, innovations and implications of learning technologies within EC–12 or teacher education contexts. Such scholarship may include, but is not limited to, studies that examine classroom-based applications of technology; youth and educators’ uses of generative AI and emerging technologies; and the use of generative AI to reimagine the nature or process of curriculum design, assessment, or teaching. We welcome applicants whose scholarship reimagines the future of education through generative AI and emerging technologies while remaining grounded in the lived experiences, cultural knowledge, and epistemologies of learners and communities. We are particularly interested in candidates who are engaged in preparing the next generation of teachers who will be able to use a range of AI and emerging technology tools to create learning experiences that are meaningful for all learners.
Strong applicants will demonstrate potential for or evidence of a significant research program that contributes to the field of Learning Technologies and has implications for educators, learners, schools, community organizations, or higher education. The successful candidate will be prepared to secure external grants to support a research program with meaningful impact.
The successful candidate will teach and mentor undergraduate students and graduate students. In Learning Technologies, a graduate program, they may teach courses in areas such as instructional design, learning theory, research methods, design-based research, online and blended learning, educational data and AI, technology-supported curriculum and instruction, and teacher education. The successful candidate will also show interest in participating in existing, or creating new, interdisciplinary collaborations that explore innovative and responsible uses of AI and Learning Technologies.
Established in 1891, the College of Education at UT Austin consistently ranks among the nation’s top public colleges of education. It is home to approximately 3,500 undergraduate and graduate students and more than 300 faculty. In addition to its longstanding commitment to academic excellence, the college has an extraordinary record of advancing innovation, opportunity, health and well-being, and educational improvement through research, teaching, and public engagement. With annual research expenditures totaling ~$60 million, the college generates knowledge with direct relevance for schools, communities, health systems, and government agencies across Texas and beyond. We also contribute to the state through the preparation of educators and health professionals and through a large network of external partnerships.
Over the past five years, the college has expanded its academic programs and enrollment. The college serves students from major metropolitan areas, smaller cities, rural regions, and border communities in Texas, while also welcoming students from other states and countries. Our students’ diverse experiences and perspectives strengthen the college’s mission to prepare educators, professionals, researchers, and leaders who can address pressing educational and community needs.
The University of Texas at Austin is the state’s leading research university, with approximately $1.3 billion in annual research expenditures and a total enrollment of more than 55,000 students. As a member of the Association of American Universities, UT Austin provides a robust ecosystem for interdisciplinary research through partnerships with Dell Medical School, the School of Social Work, and many other academic and research units on campus.
The campus is situated in Austin, one of the nation’s most dynamic and fastest-growing cities, and it is in a state that offers outstanding opportunities for scholarly inquiry. Texas is home to more than 10% of the nation’s PK–12 student population, and approximately 30% of Texas students speak a home language other than English, collectively representing more than 100 languages. Texas has also experienced significant growth in its healthcare, sports, and education sectors. Together, the scale and complexity of Texas, the dynamism of Austin, and the research strength of UT Austin offer an exceptional environment for scholars seeking to advance knowledge and improve lives.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Art History
jobs.institution: Hamilton College: Hamilton College Faculty
jobs.description:
The Art History Department at Hamilton College invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor, beginning July 1, 2027. We seek candidates with expertise in Art of the Americas before 1900; the field is open to candidates with expertise in the visual culture, material culture and/or built environment of the Americas, broadly defined as the Caribbean, North, Central and/or South America. We are especially interested in candidates whose research and teaching intersect with race and indigeneity, and can contribute to our college's interdisciplinary programs in Latin America and Latine Studies and/or American Indian and Indigenous Studies. The position requires institutional service including academic advising of undergraduate students after the first year. We are seeking candidates who can demonstrate their experience in teaching or working with broadly diverse student populations while contributing to a vibrant learning community that values academic freedom, creativity, and intellectual curiosity. Your cover letter should address the ways in which you would enhance the educational experience of students and further the College’s educational goals.
The Art History Department remains firmly committed to our goal of equipping students with a critical understanding of the historical and theoretical concerns that have shaped the production, circulation, and reception of art, visual culture, and architecture over time and around the world. This position will provide students with necessary opportunities to think critically about the structural and institutional hierarchies that have shaped the art historical discipline. A specialist in the Arts of the Americas will also sustain the department’s emphasis on object-based learning as a critical approach of the discipline and be able to take advantage of the strengths of on-campus collections at Burke Library, the College Archives, and the Wellin Museum of Art.
Candidates with ABD will be considered, although candidates with a Ph.D. are preferred. The teaching load for this position is four courses during the first year and five courses thereafter. The expected 9-month base salary range for this position is $94,500 to $100,400. Candidates should submit a cover letter, c.v., a one-page teaching statement, and the names and contact information for three references via interfolio at https://apply.interfolio.com/194151. Additional materials may be requested from applicants moving forward in the search. Questions regarding the search may be directed to Professor Arathi Menon, Search Committee Chair, at amenon@hamilton.edu. The deadline for applications is November 1, 2026.
Hamilton College is a residential liberal arts college located in central New York. The College has built its reputation on the teaching excellence and leading scholarship of its faculty, and on the academic distinction and intellectual curiosity of its approximately 2000 students who take advantage of Hamilton’s open curriculum (https://www.hamilton.edu/academics/open-curriculum). Accomplished faculty, highly capable and motivated students, and a student-faculty ratio of 9:1 provide an educational experience that emphasizes academic excellence, intellectual and cultural diversity, and respect for differences in the development of students as human beings. Hamilton’s commitment to diversity is embodied in its need-blind admission policy and meeting the full demonstrated financial need of every accepted student for their entire undergraduate program. Please visit the college website for more information (www.hamilton.edu).
Hamilton College is an affirmative action, equal opportunity employer that is committed to building an inclusive and diverse learning community where members from all backgrounds can live, learn, and excel. We encourage candidates from underrepresented groups in higher education to apply. Applicants with dual-career considerations can find other Hamilton and nearby academic job listings at https://www.hercjobs.org/regions/higher-ed-careers-upstate-new-york, as well as additional information at https://www.hamilton.edu/dof/faculty-development/resources-for-prospective-or-new-facult y/opportunities-for-spouses-or-partners (Opportunities for Spouses or Partners). jobs.title: Tirthankar Shantinath Assistant/Associate Professor in Jain Studies
jobs.institution: Rice University: School of Humanities and Arts
jobs.description:
The School of Humanities at Rice University in Houston, Texas, invites applications for the Tirthankar Shantinath Professorship in Jain Studies, with potential expertise in one or more of the following research areas: applied Jainism, bioethics, or medical humanities; or South Asian culture, religion, philosophy, or history. The position rank is open to Assistant Professors, with potential appointment at the Associate Professor level with tenure for qualified candidates. The successful candidate must qualify for an appointment in one of the departments in the School of Humanities and Arts.
Supported by a significant endowment, this chair offers a unique opportunity to establish an innovative, interdisciplinary program connecting ancient philosophical traditions with modern study of ethics, religion, philosophy, and history. The successful candidate will be an accomplished scholar of South Asian culture, history, philosophy, or religion who commands the textual languages necessary to offer dedicated courses on Jainism and direct advanced research in the field. The committee also welcomes applications from scholars with an expertise in bioethics, science, or medical practices. Key areas of scholarly engagement may also include medical ethics (such as clinical decision-making, end-of-life care, healthcare equity, genomic ethics), artificial intelligence, biotechnology, animal welfare, and planetary health.
The chairholder will play a foundational role in building the emerging field of applied Jainism, exploring how core ethical principles—specifically Ahimsa (non-violence), Aparigraha (non-possessiveness), and Anekantavada (pluralism/non-absolutism)—inform humanistic inquiry.
The successful candidate must have a Ph.D. in Jain Studies, South Asian Studies, or a related disciplinary field by July 1, 2027, and will be expected to teach and develop courses. Rice University has a semester-based teaching schedule with a 2-2 teaching load. The University expects faculty members to maintain an active program of scholarly research and publication and to contribute service to the Department, University, and profession.
Rice University is a private, comprehensive research university located in the heart of Houston’s dynamic museum district and adjacent to the Texas Medical Center. Rice University offers undergraduate and graduate degrees across eight schools and has a student body of over 4,800 undergraduates and a nearly equal number of graduate students. The fourth largest and most diverse city in the United States, Houston provides an opportunity for scholars to collaborate with area universities, museums, and civic organizations, and to engage with the broader metropolitan community.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor (One of Two Positions)
jobs.institution: New York University: Molecular Pathobiology
jobs.description:
The Department of Molecular Pathobiology at the New York University (NYU) College of Dentistry seeks applications at the level of Assistant or Associate Professor for two tenure track research-focused positions.
The Department of Molecular Pathobiology has a strong and rapidly expanding research program with substantial support from the National Institutes of Health, Department of Defense, and Foundations. The Department is located in state-of-the-art laboratories in within the broader NYU research community. Research in the Department focuses on understanding normal human biology and disease through studies of molecules, cells, tissues and systems. The Department houses the NYU Pain Research Center. Current interests include: mechanism and treatment of chronic pain; metabolic and inflammatory mechanisms and disease; receptors and signal transduction; and biomaterials, development and regenerative biology. For more information see the departmental website: https://dental.nyu.edu/faculty/molecular-pathobiology.html?challenge=d06e90d7-4d8f-4b88-9d8c-10b73beb60f1
The Department wishes to recruit highly creative scientists who will lead and maintain cutting-edge and extramurally funded research programs that will complement and synergize with current research activities in the Department of Molecular Pathobiology. The ideal candidates will interact with faculty of NYU Dentistry, NYU Langone School of Medicine, NYU Tandon School of Engineering, as well as foster collaborations with the greater NYU and New York research communities.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Psychiatry in Behavioral Sleep Medicine - Academic Clinician Track
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: Perelman School of Medicine - Psychiatry
jobs.description:
The Philadelphia VA Medical Center (PVAMC) and the Department of Psychiatry at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seek candidates for an Assistant Professor position in the non-tenure academic clinician track. Teaching responsibilities may include training and supervision of clinical psychology, trainees and staff psychologists in behavioral sleep medicine topics.
Clinical responsibilities may include provision of CBT for insomnia and other behavioral sleep services.

jobs.title: Dispatcher
jobs.institution: St. Mary's College of Maryland: Public Safety
jobs.description:
St. Mary’s College of Maryland at Historic St. Mary's City is accepting résumés for the position of Dispatcher in the Office of Public Safety. General duties include operation of radio communications equipment, dispatching routine and emergency calls for service, handling requests for service from the campus community and the general public, and acting as liaison with County and State Emergency Services. Must be able to work a rotating shift schedule or fixed shift schedule as determined by operational needs. Must be able to work weekends and holidays.
Along with the ability to handle a fast-paced environment, the successful candidate must have a high school diploma or GED equivalency, six months of related experience, familiarity with basic data entry, excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work and communicate well with students. Any combination of acceptable education and experience, which has provided the necessary knowledge and skills to fulfill the requirements of this position, may be considered. Employment will be contingent upon successful completion of a criminal background check. This is a full-time entry level position with an annual salary of $35,570, plus benefits.
St. Mary's College of Maryland, the National Public honors College, is located in Historic St. Mary's City, 70 miles southeast of Washington, D.C. St. Mary’s College is one of the nation’s best public liberal arts colleges – ranked near the top in U.S. News & World Report and a Best Value for in-state and out-of-state students. Non-sectarian since its founding, the college with its scenic waterfront campus is primarily undergraduate and residential, with a diverse coeducational student body numbering approximately 1600. The up-to-date curriculum is designed for today’s students who want an active, hands-on education led by professors who are committed teachers and experts in their fields. The quality of life is enhanced by the recreational opportunities of the Chesapeake region and close proximity to the amenities of Washington D.C., Baltimore and Richmond.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor (Two of Two Positions)

Research in the Department focuses on understanding normal human biology and disease through studies of molecules, cells, tissues and systems. The Department houses the NYU Pain Research Center. Current interests include: mechanism and treatment of chronic pain; metabolic and inflammatory mechanisms and disease; receptors and signal transduction; and biomaterials, development and regenerative biology. For more information see the departmental website: https://dental.nyu.edu/faculty/molecular-pathobiology.html?challenge=d06e90d7-4d8f-4b88-9d8c-10b73beb60f1
The Department wishes to recruit highly creative scientists who will lead and maintain cutting-edge and extramurally funded research programs that will complement and synergize with current research activities in the Department of Molecular Pathobiology. jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Linguistics

jobs.description: The Department of Linguistics at The University of Texas at Austin invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor with tenure to begin Fall of academic year 2027-2028. We seek candidates with a primary teaching and research specialization in the area of semantics and pragmatics. We are particularly interested in candidates who can interface with any of our other major areas of research in syntax, sounds, psycholinguistics, cognitive science, computational linguistics, language documentation, historical linguistics, sign language linguistics, or sociolinguistics. jobs.title: Research Scholar
jobs.institution: New York University: School of Law
jobs.description:
Trust in American institutions—government, courts, and even civil society—has steadily eroded and now stands at historic lows. In October 2025, Vanita Gupta launched the Center for Law and Public Trust at NYU School of Law to confront this crisis in confidence and reimagine US institutions so they are more effective and accountable to the American people, more resilient to corruption and abuse, and therefore more deserving of public trust.
The Center works to rebuild trust and advance effectiveness in government and other institutions by: developing issue briefs, roadmaps, and concrete blueprints for institutional reform and reconstruction; designing structures, processes, and policies that are more responsive to community needs, efficient, resilient, and accountable to the public; and training the next generation of lawyers to lead in public service, armed with the skills to deploy the levers of government and leadership, advance justice, and deliver results for the American people.
Position Summary:
The Fellow will work closely with the Center’s Director, Deputy Director, Senior Fellows, and Distinguished Scholars in Residence to contribute to rigorous, high-impact legal work in the public interest. For this particular position, the Center is seeking someone who will work on our accountability and anti-corruption portfolio. The Center is therefore particularly interested in candidates with a background in these areas.
The Fellow will perform a wide range of research, writing, and project management tasks, including, but not limited to:
Conducting research on matters relevant to the Center’s projects and initiatives
Supporting and coordinating outreach, meetings and convenings with subject matter experts and partner organizations
Generating scholarship around the Center’s areas of expertise
Writing all types of materials, from internal research memos and talking points to public-facing reports
Building tools and templates, analyzing and synthesizing inputs and information, and helping to create and refine key deliverables for Center projects.
Managing lines of effort and providing logistical support to various projects to ensure milestones are met and deliverables are completed on time.
Advising Center leadership, staff, and fellows and acting as a thought partner based on the scholar’s expertise and experience.
As needed, supervising student researchers to produce deliverables and complete tasks, ensuring quality and timeliness.
Representing the Center at coalition meetings, conferences, convenings, and other public events, as appropriate
Building and maintaining strong relationships with senior practitioners, academics, experts, and counterparts across the University and at partner organizations.
Salary and Benefits
In compliance with NYC's Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary is $150,000. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer. You will be an employee of New York University, with access to an excellent, comprehensive benefits package including generous paid time off and retirement contributions.
The Center has physical office space at NYU School of Law in New York, but also offers hybrid or remote work arrangements from within the US.

jobs.title: Experiential Program Coordinator, Gateway Career Center
jobs.institution: Lafayette College: Provost
jobs.description:
The Experiential Program Coordinator, Gateway Career Center manages the operations, logistics, and data tracking that connect Lafayette College students with experiential learning and employment opportunities.
Reporting to the Associate Director, Employer Relations and Experiential Learning, the Experiential Program Coordinator manages day-to-day recruitment systems, executes major campus recruiting events, supports the development, administration, and execution of experiential learning programs, manages specialized experiential cohorts, and oversees the Federal Work Study (FWS) campus employment workflow.
Key Responsibilities
Experiential Learning Program Support
• Program Logistics & Delivery: Support the operational execution, cohort registration, and scheduling for high-impact external programs, including Training the Street and Podium.
• New Program Vetting: Review and research incoming proposals for new experiential learning opportunities and vendor partnerships to verify legitimacy, rigor, and strategic relevance to liberal arts student interests.
• Development Collaboration: Support the development of new experiential learning initiatives by collaborating with internal campus stakeholders, alumni, and external partners to establish program workflows and application timelines.
• Student Tracking & Reporting: Systematically track student application, completion, and performance data across all specialized experiential programs, updating tracking fields within Handshake and generating outcome summaries for leadership.
• Cohort Outreach: Coordinate marketing campaigns and informational outreach to students and staff to drive engagement, equity, and diverse participation in both new and existing experiential opportunities.
Recruiting Operations & Data Management
• Application & Data Integrity: Manage the student application process for positions posted in Handshake, ensuring the data integrity, completeness, and accuracy of required tracking fields.
• Employer Tracking & Reporting: Track all employer contacts, utilized services, and recruitment actions; systematically collect student performance and job-offer data to generate opportunity and outcomes reports for leadership.
• CRM Management: Maintain and monitor recruiting operational data and alumni, parent, and employer contact information utilizing Handshake and CRM system.
• Vetting & Curation: Review and research incoming employer inquiries, full-time positions, internships, and interview schedules within Handshake to verify validity, legitimacy, accuracy, and relevance to student interests.
• Communication: Frequently communicate with Associate Director and Sr. Associate Director regarding incoming employer and alumni inquiries and assign to team members for follow-up and relationship development based on industry areas of expertise.
Event & Career Fair Logistics
• Career Fair Coordination: Coordinate full career fair logistics under the direction of the Associate Director, Employer Relations and Experiential Learning: process registrations, track payments, issue confirmation emails, design table layouts, build student programs, and establish staff schedules.
• Campus Event Liaison: Serve as the central operational liaison with campus departments (Catering, Facilities, Public Safety) to coordinate room setups, food and beverage needs, and parking logistics for large-scale events.
• Recruitment Scheduling: Coordinate the primary calendar and schedule for all fall and spring on-campus and virtual recruiting cycles.
• Employer Information Sessions: Coordinate Employer Information Sessions, including room reservations, platform postings, marketing to students/staff, and arranging student event coverage.
• On-Campus Visit Logistics: Oversee the logistics of incoming recruiting visits, providing employers with candidate resumes, campus directions, and interview schedules, and greet employers upon arrival.
• Targeted Outreach: Collaborate with the Employer Relations team to generate career fair invitation lists (incorporating historical attendee lists) and align outreach to managed employer accounts.
Federal Work Study (FWS) Management
• Seasonal Outreach: Coordinate seasonal outreach per the FWS timeline to faculty, staff, and campus departments to collect and post Work Study/Campus Job Employment (CJE) vacancies into Handshake.
• Financial Aid Collaboration: Collaborate directly with the Financial Aid office to ensure accurate FWS information dissemination and timely outreach to students and supervisors.
• Campus Point of Contact: Act as the primary campus point of contact for questions, regularly communicating with campus supervisors regarding hiring policies and eligible students regarding application workflows.

jobs.title: Open Rank Position in Music Education, Natalie L. Haslam College of Music, Fall 2027
jobs.institution: The University of Tennessee - Knoxville: Natalie L. Haslam College of Music
jobs.description:
Assistant, Associate or Full Professor; nine-month tenure-track appointment beginning Fall Semester, August 1, 2027. Salary and fringe benefits are competitive and commensurate with rank and experience.
The University of Tennessee's Natalie L. Haslam College of Music is seeking a dynamic music educator to join our faculty. The ideal candidate will demonstrate a collaborative spirit, bring expertise in elementary/general music education and contribute to our undergraduate and graduate music education offerings. The candidate should work collaboratively with other College of Music faculty to sustain and support the music education program, maintain a research/creative/scholarly activity profile commensurate with appointed rank, and demonstrate a commitment to forward-thinking curriculum development, innovation, and community engagement.
Primary responsibilities include teaching undergraduates in elementary music education, leading graduate courses in areas of expertise, coordinating field experience internships, and supervising student teachers/interns. The successful candidate will actively participate in professional development for elementary/general music educators, develop regional and national visibility as an elementary/general music educator, and develop and maintain positive relationships with inservice music educators. The candidate is also expected to serve on graduate committees and participate in various education and professional development opportunities including TMEA (ETGMEA), CNAfME, and NAfME.
Web Page: music.utk.edu
The University of Tennessee Natalie L. Haslam College of Music offers a broad and comprehensive professional music program at both the undergraduate and graduate levels and is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music. The College has approximately 65 faculty members and approximately 400 music majors.
General Information:
The University of Tennessee, Knoxville, is the state’s flagship research institution, a campus of choice for outstanding undergraduates, and a premier graduate institution. As a land-grant university, it is committed to excellence in learning, scholarship, and engagement with society. In all its activities, the university aims to advance the frontiers of human knowledge and enrich and elevate society. Knoxville’s cultural resources include a symphony orchestra, an opera company, a professional jazz orchestra, theatrical productions, ballet and modern dance, art galleries, and museums. Within an hour’s drive is the Great Smoky Mountains National Park with its scenic beauty and wide variety of recreational activities, plants, and wildlife.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Community-Engaged Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Implementation Science - PH 358
jobs.institution: Brown University: Behavioral and Social Sciences
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Associate (100% FTE for a minimum of 2 years) to advance community-engaged research in nutrition, physical activity, implementation science, and chronic disease prevention. The postdoctoral scholar will be affiliated with the Center for Health Promotion and Health Equity (CHPHE) at the Brown University School of Public Health.
This mentored postdoctoral position is designed to support the development of an independent research trajectory in intervention science, implementation science, and community-engaged research aimed at improving health outcomes and health equity. The postdoc will join a major NIH-funded R01 study, "Evaluating a Statewide Community Intervention Model to Address Cardiovascular Risk, Diet, and Physical Activity," led by Drs. Alison Tovar and Lauren Bohlen. This research evaluates Rhode Island's pioneering Community Intermediary Organization / Health Equity Zone (HEZ) model across 14 local communities to establish data-driven, scalable solutions for community-based chronic disease prevention, healthy eating, and physical activity promotion. The postdoc will join an active, collaborative research environment spanning school districts, community organizations, state agencies, and regional and national partners.
Training Environment and Career Development
The postdoctoral associate will receive structured mentorship from Drs. Tovar & Bohlen and collaborating faculty and will be supported in:
Developing an independent line of research within community engaged research focused on nutrition and/or physical activity
Publishing first-authored manuscripts in high-impact peer-reviewed journals
Gaining advanced training, including structured didactics, in multi-level intervention design, evaluation methodologies, implementation science, and community-engaged research approaches
Preparing competitive career development awards (e.g., NIH K-series, foundation awards)
Contributing to and leading components of NIH and foundation grant submissions
Presenting research at national and international scientific meetings
The postdoctoral scholar will have opportunities to engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across Brown University, CHPHE, and partner institutions, and to participate in consortium-building efforts focused on community-based nutrition and physical activity research.
Responsibilities
Contribute to the design, implementation, data collection, and evaluation of multi-level community- and school-based nutrition and physical activity interventions
Conduct quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods data analyses on dietary quality, physical activity, cardiovascular risk factors, and implementation outcomes
Lead and contribute to peer-reviewed publications derived from grant datasets
Assist with development of federal (NIH, USDA) and foundation grant applications
Support community partnerships, Health Equity Zone networks, and stakeholder engagement across HEZ sites
Contribute to dissemination of findings to academic, policy, and community audiences
Appointment Details
The initial appointment is for 2 years, with potential renewal contingent upon performance and funding availability. Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience and includes a comprehensive benefits package.
Work Location
This job posting is for an in-person postdoctoral research associate, who will have the option to work in a hybrid format.
Brown University is a registered employer in the following states: Rhode Island, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Maryland, Massachusetts, New York, New Hampshire, New Jersey, North Carolina, Washington, D.C. All remote work must be performed in a state in which Brown is registered to do business.
Visas
For this position, Brown offers only the J-1 visa classification to scholars who need immigration sponsorship in order to enter the U.S. and commence lawful employment under the terms of their appointment.

jobs.title: Open Rank/Open Tenure - Small Animal Educator, Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
jobs.institution: Clemson University: Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
jobs.location: CVM - COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE HUB(001184) BLDG001184
jobs.description:
The Clemson University Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine (PCVM) is seeking applicants for several full-time positions to serve as Small Animal Educators. These faculty positions will play a pivotal role in the development and implementation of the Clemson DVM curriculum (https://www.clemson.edu/veterinary-medicine/students/curriculum.html). The successful candidates will have a primary instructional role in developing and delivering small animal medicine and / or surgery content in the integrated Clemson DVM curriculum. These faculty members will teach with a dynamic, collaborative team consisting of experienced general practice clinicians, boarded specialists, and education specialists. The small animal medicine and surgery course series is designed to be an integrated, systems-based approach for conditions common to small animal general practice. This role is designed to attract outstanding educators and experienced clinicians who are passionate about teaching diagnostic medicine and small animal surgery in a practical, integrated fashion. Board certification in small animal internal medicine, small animal surgery, or ABVP certification is encouraged but not required.
The Clemson DVM curriculum is based upon integrative, collaborative team teaching in which faculty with varying backgrounds can work together to offer students an inclusive and innovative learning environment. The Small Animal Educators will collaborate with our other teaching faculty to facilitate vertical and horizontal integration for the delivery of core small animal internal medicine and surgery principles. Utilizing state of the art classrooms and teaching technology, this faculty member will be asked to adopt an integrated educational approach to provide students with a strong foundation of cognitive, clinical, and professional competencies in preparation for entry into the partially distributive model of clinical training in the fourth year. This position will consist primarily of didactic and small group instruction, along with some instruction in teaching laboratories. While the PCVM will not have a specialty referral hospital, it will have a fully staffed Community Practice as well as a robust Shelter Medicine spay-neuter program. The Small Animal Educators will work closely with the Community Practice and Shelter Medicine clinicians to integrate classroom concepts that translate seamlessly into real world experiences. A clinical service commitment is not required; however, interested individuals are encouraged to engage in teaching activities in our Community Practice. Additionally, these faculty members will engage in scholarly activity, which can include curriculum development, programmatic or curricular assessment, scholarship of teaching and learning, and other similar activities. Finally, a hybrid academic appointment will be considered for a boarded small animal specialist (internal medicine and / or surgery). If desired, this individual may seek a combination of a part-time academic appointment at Clemson while also having a part-time position in private referral practice. The possibility of a 9-month to 12-month contract are options that can be discussed with the Department Chair.
Overview of Clemson and the PCVM
Located in South Carolina’s beautiful and fast-growing Upstate, Clemson University is the land-grant university of South Carolina and ranks among the country’s top 50 national public universities in the U.S. News & World Report. The University has nearly 23,400 students (including nearly 18,600 undergraduates) who can select from 80 undergraduate and 110 graduate degree programs. Clemson employs over 1,150 full-time faculty and has an annual budget expenditure of over $900M. Clemson University maintains its status as an R1 Carnegie Research Institution while maintaining a strong focus on undergraduate education.
The PCVM is currently seeking accreditation by the American Veterinary Medicine Association-Council on Education to offer the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree to approximately 80 students per cohort which started in August 2026). The PCVM plans to utilize a partial distributive model of clinical training for students. Its brand-new state of the art campus will reside in Pendleton, SC, near the T. Ed Garrison Arena, will house research and teaching labs, and utilize both ambulatory services as well as teaching sites at the Clemson University Equine Center, Lamaster Dairy Cattle Center, and other locations for education in the field.
In 2023, the Board of Trustees approved Clemson Elevate, the university’s new strategic plan. Clemson Elevate is built on 3 pillars: deliver the #1 student experience, double research by 2035, and transform lives statewide and beyond. The PCVM was named as a strategic priority for the university, demonstrating the importance of the new college to the future of the university and the state. We are excited to attract a team of top talent as we build the new college.
Overview of the Position
Reporting to the Department Chair and working closely with the Foundational Sciences and Clinical Skills Leads, the small animal medicine educator will:
Create and deliver the small animal content in the team-taught systems-based courses in the curriculum.
Participate in teaching laboratories as agreed upon with colleagues and the department chair
Develop assessment strategies in alignment with the overall competency-based curriculum.
Collaborate with other faculty members to ensure integration of knowledge and skills across years and courses.
Actively and effectively engage in student-centered instruction, coaching, and mentorship.
Collaborate closely with the Clemson University Community Practice and with our partner clinics.
Serve on PCVM and campus committees as an appointed or elected member.
Additionally, the faculty member must have the ability to:
Emulate our PCVM cultural values including integrity, authenticity, respect, welcoming, trust, and collaboration.
Work independently and collaboratively as part of a team, possess exemplary verbal and written communication skills, with exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.
Prioritize and manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and function independently with limited supervision and guidance.
Work in partnership with faculty and staff across multiple disciplines and functions across the college and university.
Participate in research and scholarship initiatives designed to improve educational and professional outcomes.
Demonstrate a commitment to the core values of Clemson University and specifically to community, engagement, belonging and accessibility (CEBA).

jobs.title: Student Assistant for Digitization

jobs.title: Campaign Director
jobs.institution: Lafayette College: Advancement
jobs.description:
The Campaign Director is a senior advancement professional responsible for the strategic planning, execution, and management of Lafayette College’s comprehensive capital campaign. This role will focus on behind-the-scenes systems, timelines, and volunteer coordination, as well as support for the VP on operational strategy and frontline principal gift fundraising.
Position Summary
The Fundraising Campaign Director provides strategic leadership and administrative oversight for the College’s comprehensive fundraising campaign. Reporting to the Vice President for Advancement, this individual collaborates closely with the College President, Board of Trustees, Provost, senior development staff, and consultants. The Director ensures that the campaign moves on schedule, remains aligned with institutional priorities, and achieves its financial goals.

1. Strategic Campaign Planning & Management
● Develop the Campaign Blueprint: Design and execute the multi-year campaign plan, including high-level timelines, operational benchmarks, performance milestones, and specific deliverables.
● Complete and expand Case Statements and Marketing Support: Partner with senior leaders and academic stakeholders to draft the overarching case for support and campaign messaging frameworks.

● Campaign Communications: Collaborate with the College Communications and Advancement Marketing teams to oversee the development of specialized donor collateral, campaign web platforms, and public launch events.
4. Portfolio Management & Gift Solicitation (Varies by Institution)

● Leadership Support: Accompany the Vice President on donor visits, providing strategic briefing materials beforehand.

jobs.title: Tenure-track Assistant Professor of Creative Writing and Writer in Residence
jobs.institution: Connecticut College: English
jobs.description:
The English Department of Connecticut College seeks an Assistant Professor and Writer in Residence specializing in prose fiction and/or nonfiction writing to begin on July 1, 2027. The position comes with a competitive salary and is eligible for benefits. An MFA or Ph.D. is required for appointment. We are a department of ten faculty members with a broad range of commitments to interdisciplinary programs and centers on campus, including the Center for the Comparative Study of Race and Ethnicity; the Ammerman Center for Arts and Technology; American Studies; Environmental Studies; the department of Gender, Sexuality, and Intersectionality Studies; and others. All faculty teach courses at all levels.
The successful candidate will join a thriving program in Creative Writing as one of two full-time Writers in Residence. (The other is our Poet in Residence.) Our program in Creative Writing is a valuable part of the English major, and Fiction and Nonfiction writing courses are very much in demand among our students. Our student writers take Creative Writing courses alongside literature courses, and they benefit from one-on-one mentoring relationships with our Writers in Residence. We are proud of the success of this program, which has launched many careers. Creative writing events on campus include the biennial Daniel Klagsbrun Symposium [embed the link: https://www.conncoll.edu/news/news-archive/2019/daniel-klagsbrun-symposium/] and other events and readings by writers including Jhumpa Lahiri, Ocean Vuong, Amy Tan, David Sedaris, and Art Spiegelman, and readings by students. The successful candidate will collaborate with English department faculty to organize readings and other Creative Writing events.
Courses taught by the person hired for this position may include Writing the Short Story, Seminar in Fiction, and Narrative Nonfiction and Creative Writing courses of their own design. Advising student honors theses in fiction or nonfiction writing is also expected.
In addition to vibrant connections within the English major, the successful candidate may benefit from collaboration with other Arts programs on campus, including Studio Art, Music, Theater, and Film.
Tenure-track faculty members teach a 3-2 load (2-2 in the first year). In addition to providing ongoing strong support for teaching and research, the College offers the following resources for pre-tenured faculty: a supplementary research fund and a semester’s sabbatical at full salary after a successful third-year review. (For additional information on faculty resources, see http://www.conncoll.edu/employment/faculty-resources/).

jobs.title: Assistant Scientist (Exemplars in Global Health: Large-Scale Food Fortification)
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: Department of International Health
jobs.location: School of Public Health, 615 N. Wolfe Street, Baltimore, MD 21205
jobs.description:
Background:
The Institute for International Programs at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health is a network of scientists focused on improving the quality of information available to support public health policies and decision-making in maternal and child health and nutrition across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).
We seek a faculty member at the rank of Assistant Scientist (non-tenure track) to work on an Exemplars in Global Health (EGH) study focused on large-scale food fortification (LSFF). EGH is a research initiative that uses a positive deviance approach to identify countries that have achieved exceptional progress on key health and nutrition outcomes or interventions, understand the drivers of that success, and translate findings into actionable guidance for global health decision makers. The EGH LSFF study will consist of 5–6 in-depth, mixed-methods country case studies examining the factors that have enabled successful LSFF programs.
As an Assistant Scientist on this project, you will be responsible for the scientific and technical direction of this study, including development of the study design and methodology, data sourcing, development of data collection tools, support with qualitative data collection and analysis, and quantitative data management and analysis. You will provide technical assistance to in-country research teams across the 5–6 country case studies and lead overall project coordination to ensure the study meets its objectives on time. This role involves direct engagement with the funder and in-country partners, and leadership of dissemination materials (e.g., technical notes, guidance documents, and multi-country publications) to ensure study findings inform food fortification policy and programming. You will also actively engage colleagues and partners working on related studies for the purpose of learning and collaboration.
You will work closely with the Principal Investigator (PI) and co-investigators to refine and implement the study’s vision, goals, and objectives. You are responsible for coordinating cross-partner workflows; liaising with the funder and in-country partners; responding to donor and other requests for
information; and ensuring all study activities and deliverables are completed on time and to a high standard.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Applied Research and Technical Assistance (40%)
· Lead the design of the mixed-methods study protocol for the country case studies, including development of research questions, sampling strategies, and data collection tools along with identification of data sources; this will include adapting methods across the 5-6 selected country-programs.
· Identify and prioritize research questions and lead design of quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis strategies across individual country case studies.
· Lead quantitative data analysis activities, including primary and secondary data analysis, to identify drivers of program performance across countries.
· Oversee synthesis of case study findings into cross-country comparative analyses and project-related outputs, including technical reports and scientific articles.
· Prepares documentation for IRB submissions across all study sites.
Program/Project Management (40%)
· Coordinate and co-facilitate in-country study inception and dissemination meetings.
· Coordinate development and management of study workplans, timelines, and deliverables across country case studies to ensure the study meets its objectives on time.
· Serve as primary liaison with the funder, providing regular progress updates and reports, and coordinating responses to donor requests for information.
· Liaise with in-country partners and country case study teams to coordinate cross-partner workflows and support achievement of high-quality, timely project deliverables.
· Assist with development of contract deliverable schedules and scopes of work, and other documents necessary to secure approval and execute partner awards. Once awarded, track progress and coordinate technical updates to ensure invoice payment.
· Engage with internal and external subject matter experts to solicit timely technical support as needed.
· Coordinate and co-facilitate regular meetings of country teams, core partners, the funder, and the PI/co-investigators.
· Engage with the JHU Finance Team in budget development, financial tracking, and financial reporting. Advise the PI concerning major expenditures, spending priorities, and planning.
Communication and Knowledge Management (20%)
· Lead development of dissemination materials, including technical reports, briefs, manuscripts, and presentations summarizing study findings for the funder, policymakers, and academic audiences.
· Design and deliver presentations at workshops, conferences, and working groups; support the PI in preparing presentations for diverse audiences including the funder, in-country partners, and technical working groups.
· Coordinate editing, layout, and/or translation support as required for dissemination products.
Required Skills and Experience:
· Doctoral degree (PhD, ScD, DrPH, or equivalent) in public health, nutrition, economics, or a related field plus at least 2 years of relevant post-doctoral experience; or a Master’s degree in a relevant field plus at least 6 years of relevant work experience.
· Demonstrated understanding of large-scale food fortification programs, micronutrient malnutrition, or related public health nutrition topics.
· Demonstrated experience independently designing and leading mixed-methods research, including in-depth case study methodology, in LMICs.
· Advanced quantitative data analysis skills, including experience with statistical software (e.g., Stata, R) and secondary/large dataset analysis.
· Knowledge of qualitative methods is an asset.
· Project management experience including development and tracking of workplans, financial management, and multi-country stakeholder coordination.
· Experience liaising with funders and donors, including preparation of progress reports and responses to donor requests.
· Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, including experience translating complex technical material and research findings into dissemination-friendly formats.
· Strong interpersonal skills and social-emotional intelligence; experience working with cross-cultural teams and a range of in-country partners, including government, implementing partners, and local/academic organizations in LMICs.
· Ability to work independently, exercise sound scientific judgment, and manage a complex, multi-country workload under tight timelines, as part of a matrixed global team.
· Ability to prioritize workload, assume responsibility for work, and follow tasks through to completion.
· Availability to travel internationally approximately 20%.

jobs.title: Associate or Full Professor of Curriculum and Instruction with a Specialization in Learning Technologies
jobs.institution: The University of Texas at Austin: Department of Curriculum & Instruction
jobs.description:
The Department of Curriculum and Instruction in the College of Education at The University of Texas at Austin seeks a faculty member at the associate professor or full professor level whose scholarship advances Learning Technologies. Although the primary appointment falls within the Learning Technologies program area in the Department of Curriculum and Instruction, the successful candidate will have the ability to lead college-wide initiatives related to Learning Technologies. A secondary appointment in the Department of Kinesiology and Health Education, Special Education, Educational Psychology, or Educational Leadership and Policy will also be considered.
The successful candidate will have a strong record of research focusing on the applications, implications, and innovations of Learning Technologies in EC–12, higher education, professional learning, or informal contexts. Such scholarship may include, but is not limited to, studies of generative AI in teaching and learning; learning analytics and educational data science; human-AI interaction; the design of AI- and technology-enriched learning environments; technology-supported curriculum design and assessment; technology-rich teacher education and professional learning; and accessible, culturally responsive, and community-engaged learning technologies. We welcome scholarship that advances educational innovations while critically examining the pedagogical, ethical, social, cultural, and policy implications of AI and emerging technologies.
We especially welcome applicants whose work reimagines the future of education through responsible uses of AI and digital technologies while remaining attentive to the diverse contexts in which teaching and learning occur. The successful candidate will have a record of securing external grants to support a research program with meaningful impact.
The successful candidate will teach and mentor undergraduate students and graduate students. In Learning Technologies, a graduate program, they may teach courses in areas such as instructional design, learning theory, research methods, design-based research, online and blended learning, educational data and AI, technology-supported curriculum and instruction, and teacher education. The successful candidate will also show interest in participating in existing, or creating new, interdisciplinary collaborations that explore innovative and responsible uses of AI and Learning Technologies.
Established in 1891, the College of Education at UT Austin consistently ranks among the nation’s top public colleges of education. It is home to approximately 3,500 undergraduate and graduate students and more than 300 faculty. In addition to its longstanding commitment to academic excellence, the college has an extraordinary record of advancing innovation, opportunity, health and well-being, and educational improvement through research, teaching, and public engagement. With annual research expenditures totaling ~$60 million, the college generates knowledge with direct relevance for schools, communities, health systems, and government agencies across Texas and beyond. We also contribute to the state through the preparation of educators and health professionals and through a large network of external partnerships.
Over the past five years, the college has expanded its academic programs and enrollment. The college serves students from major metropolitan areas, smaller cities, rural regions, and border communities in Texas, while also welcoming students from other states and countries. Our students’ diverse experiences and perspectives strengthen the college’s mission to prepare educators, professionals, researchers, and leaders who can address pressing educational and community needs.
The University of Texas at Austin is the state’s leading research university, with approximately $1.3 billion in annual research expenditures and a total enrollment of more than 55,000 students. As a member of the Association of American Universities, UT Austin provides a robust ecosystem for interdisciplinary research through partnerships with Dell Medical School, the School of Social Work, and many other academic and research units on campus.
The campus is situated in Austin, one of the nation’s most dynamic and fastest-growing cities, and it is in a state that offers outstanding opportunities for scholarly inquiry. Texas is home to more than 10% of the nation’s PK–12 student population, and approximately 30% of Texas students speak a home language other than English, collectively representing more than 100 languages. Texas has also experienced significant growth in its healthcare, sports, and education sectors. Together, the scale and complexity of Texas, the dynamism of Austin, and the research strength of UT Austin offer an exceptional environment for scholars seeking to advance knowledge and improve lives.

The University invites applications and nominations for the position of Head of the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering.
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) is a world-class university known for its innovative education, research excellence, and impactful knowledge transfer. With a holistic and interdisciplinary pedagogy approach, HKUST was ranked 6th in the QS Asia University Rankings 2026, 3rd in the Times Higher Education’s Young University Rankings 2026, and 20th globally and 1st in Hong Kong in the Times Higher Education’s Impact Rankings 2026. Eleven HKUST subjects were ranked among the world’s top 50 in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026, with “Civil and Structural Engineering” coming in 27th worldwide. Our graduates are highly competitive, consistently ranking among the world’s top 30 most sought-after employees. As of January 2026, HKUST members have founded over 1,900 active start-ups, including 10 Unicorns and 21 exits (IPO or M&A).
The Department
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CIVL) at HKUST invites applications from outstanding candidates with the vision, energy, and leadership potential to help shape the next stage of the Department’s development.
CIVL comprises more than 35 faculty members and serves approximately 480 undergraduate students and 300 postgraduate research students. The Department offers BEng, MSc, MPhil, and PhD programs. The Department conducts comprehensive teaching and research across fundamental and applied areas of civil and environmental engineering.
Building on HKUST’s strengths in science, engineering, innovation, and interdisciplinary collaborations, CIVL seeks to tackle pressing global and regional challenges in building smart, resilient, sustainable, healthy and inclusive communities. Its expertise spans infrastructure resilience, climate adaptation, sustainable urban systems, environmental protection, water resources, geotechnical and structural engineering, transportation, autonomous construction technology, and the digital transformation of built environment.
The Department is supported by a wide range of research platforms, advanced laboratories, and experimental, computational, and field research capabilities, featuring a State Key Laboratory and a Chinese National Engineering Research Center, and having launched the Hong Kong’s first satellite. CIVL has established strengths in sensing, monitoring, data analytics, and digital and space technologies for civil and environmental engineering applications. The Department also benefits from partnerships with industry, and has a strong record of competitive funding, professional engagement, and societal impact.
We seek candidates who can bring a bold, forward-looking, and inclusive academic vision; strengthen existing areas of excellence; open new interdisciplinary directions; and contribute to CIVL’s continued development in research, education, knowledge transfer, and global engagement. The successful candidate is expected to help enhance the Department’s academic reputation, attract and mentor outstanding students and faculty, foster collaboration across disciplines, and advance CIVL’s standing as a world-leading, innovative department in Hong Kong, the Greater Bay Area, and beyond.
The Role & Terms
Reporting to the Dean of Engineering, the Head of CIVL is expected to provide leadership for the Department and manage its diverse academic and administrative functions.
Concurrent with a tenured professorial appointment, the Head appointment will typically be for an initial 3-year term and may be renewable for a second term. Competitive remuneration and generous fringe benefits, including housing where appropriate, will be provided.

jobs.title: Research Associate / Research Scientist of Advanced Radar Research Center
jobs.institution: University of Oklahoma Norman Campus: Advanced Radar Research Center
jobs.description:
The University of Oklahoma has an opening for a Research Associate or Research Scientist in advanced radar signal processing, electromagnetic/radio-frequency interference (EMI/RFI) mitigation, and phased array radar (PAR). Appointment level will be commensurate with education and experience: candidates with an M.S. will be considered at the Research Associate level, while candidates with a Ph.D. will be considered at the Research Scientist level.
The primary focus will be development, implementation, and evaluation of signal-processing algorithms to detect, characterize, and mitigate external interference in weather-radar data. The successful candidate will work with simulated and measured complex I/Q data; develop interference detection, excision, filtering, estimation, and mitigation methods; and quantify effects on radar data quality, including reflectivity, radial velocity, spectrum width, and dual-polarization variables. The work will emphasize rigorous, reproducible evaluation over a range of interference levels, radar operating modes, and weather/ground-clutter conditions.
The candidate will also contribute to phased array radar analyses relevant to spectrum-efficient weather-radar operation. Depending on background and project needs, topics may include the following: array signal processing, digital beamforming, adaptive nulling, frequency/waveform agility, spectral-footprint characterization, and trade studies involving update rate, sensitivity, interference susceptibility, and spectrum coexistence. The position will involve close collaboration with OU/ARRC radar engineers and scientists and NOAA/NWS technical partners, with access to radar testbeds, high-performance computing resources, and extensive weather-radar datasets.
The successful candidate will work primarily in the Radar Innovations Laboratory and National Weather Center in Norman, Oklahoma, in a highly collaborative environment involving OU faculty, engineers, students, NOAA scientists, and other federal and industry partners. jobs.title: Research Associate – Child and Adolescent Causes of Death Estimation Project 2.0 (CA-CODE 2.0)
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: Department of International Health
jobs.description:
Background
The Institute for International Programs at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health is a network of investigators focused on improving the quality and use of information to support public health policies and decision-making in maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health across low- and middle-income countries.
The Child and Adolescent Causes of Death Estimation project, or CA-CODE, supports the generation, improvement, harmonization, interpretation, and use of newborn, child, and adolescent cause-of-death estimates at national, regional, and global levels. The previous phase of CA-CODE included work related to methodological innovation, country engagement, estimates harmonization, evidence exploration, and dissemination, including development and maintenance of a data portal to facilitate engagement with country and global partners.
CA-CODE 2.0 will build upon this work by advancing the evidence base, data systems, analytic methods, and partnerships needed to produce and use high-quality child and adolescent cause-of-death information.
Position Summary
We seek a full-time faculty member at the rank of Research Associate to provide research program coordination and technical support for CA-CODE 2.0. The Research Associate will work closely with the Principal Investigators, co-investigators, research staff, and collaborating institutions to support the implementation of the project’s scientific and operational activities. The Research Associate will receive ongoing supervision and support from senior investigators and other experienced team members.
The position will combine general research program coordination with substantial technical responsibilities related to database management, data quality assurance, statistical analysis, systematic reviews, and preparation of scientific and programmatic products. The Research Associate will help coordinate activities across project partners and workstreams while also contributing directly to data management, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination. The position is expected to be primarily on site initially, with the possibility of periodic remote work once a track record of productivity has been established.
Roles and Responsibilities
Research Program Coordination – approximately 35%
• Participate in strategic planning and development of project objectives, activities, timelines, and deliverables.
• Develop, maintain, and monitor integrated workplans across CA-CODE 2.0 workstreams and collaborating institutions.
• Coordinate cross-partner workflows and help ensure that scientific, technical, and administrative activities remain aligned with project objectives.
• Monitor progress toward milestones and deliverables through regular check-ins, progress reports, action trackers, and other project-management tools.
• Coordinate regular meetings of investigators, technical working groups, country partners, and other collaborators, including preparing agendas, documenting decisions, and tracking action items.
• Facilitate communication and knowledge sharing across project teams and identify opportunities to strengthen coordination, efficiency, and performance.
• Coordinate preparation of annual reports, technical updates, donor deliverables, meeting reports, and responses to requests for information from donors.
• Support the development and monitoring of scopes of work, deliverable schedules, and technical components of agreements with collaborating institutions.
• Coordinate with BSPH administrative, finance, grants, and contracts teams as needed.
• Support ethical review submissions, data-use agreements, research documentation, and compliance with institutional and project requirements.
• Assist with the planning and implementation of technical meetings, workshops, webinars, and dissemination activities.
Database and Data Management – approximately 25%
• Develop and maintain well-organized project databases containing mortality, cause-of-death, demographic, health-system, and other relevant data.
• Coordinate the receipt, inventory, storage, cleaning, harmonization, linkage, and documentation of datasets obtained from multiple countries and partner organizations.
• Develop and maintain data dictionaries, variable crosswalks, metadata, standard operating procedures, and database-management documentation.
• Implement routine data-quality checks to identify missingness, inconsistencies, duplicate records, coding problems, and other data-quality concerns.
• Work with investigators and partner organizations to resolve data-quality issues and document all decisions and revisions.
• Maintain clear dataset and analytic version-control systems and support reproducible data-management workflows.
• Prepare analysis-ready datasets in accordance with approved analysis plans.
• Support appropriate data-access, confidentiality, security, backup, archiving, and data-governance procedures.
• Provide technical guidance and support to research staff and partners contributing data to the project.
Data Analysis and Interpretation – approximately 15%
• Collaborate with investigators to develop and refine statistical analysis plans.
• Conduct descriptive and inferential analyses of newborn, child, and adolescent mortality and cause-of-death data.
• Support analyses comparing estimates across data sources, geographic settings, age groups, time periods, and estimation approaches.
• Contribute to analyses of data quality, completeness, comparability, misclassification, and uncertainty.
• Develop reproducible analytic code and maintain clear documentation of analytic procedures.
• Generate publication-quality tables, figures, dashboards, and other data products.
• Review and validate analytic results and work with investigators to interpret findings.
• Contribute to sensitivity analyses and other assessments of the robustness of findings.
• Prepare analytic summaries for investigators, partners, technical working groups, funders, and other audiences.
• Contribute to the preparation of abstracts, presentations, technical reports, policy products, and peer-reviewed manuscripts.
Systematic Reviews and Scientific Dissemination – approximately 25%
• Develop protocols for systematic, scoping, or rapid reviews relevant to child and adolescent mortality and cause-of-death estimation.
• Develop and implement database search strategies in collaboration with investigators and information specialists.
• Coordinate citation management, duplicate removal, title and abstract screening, full-text screening, and study selection.
• Develop and pilot standardized data-extraction tools.
• Extract, clean, organize, and synthesize information from peer-reviewed and grey literature.
• Conduct quality, methodological, or risk-of-bias assessments, as appropriate to the review design.
• Maintain review documentation and support adherence to relevant reporting standards, including PRISMA guidance where applicable.
• Conduct narrative, quantitative, or other evidence syntheses, depending on the available literature.
• Prepare evidence tables, figures, technical summaries, manuscripts, presentations, and other dissemination products.
