jobs.institution: The Ohio State University: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
jobs.description:
Tenure-Track Assistant Professor of Artificial Intelligence for Chemical, Materials, and Manufacturing Engineering
William G. Lowrie Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering and Department of Materials Science and Engineering
College of Engineering
The William G. Lowrie Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (https://cbe.osu.edu/) and the Department of Materials Science and Engineering (https://mse.osu.edu) at The Ohio State University invite applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor in the area of Artificial Intelligence. This is a joint appointment with a 70% tenure-home appointment in Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering and a 30% appointment in Materials Science and Engineering. The anticipated start date is August 2027, although a later start date may be negotiated.
This position is part of Ohio State's strategic investment in Artificial Intelligence and seeks candidates whose research advances the development and/or application of AI methodologies that accelerate scientific discovery, engineering design, manufacturing, decision-making, and innovation. We welcome candidates conducting research that spans foundational AI, scientific machine learning, and AI-enabled engineering applications.
The successful candidate will develop innovative research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and engineering disciplines relevant to chemical engineering, materials science, manufacturing, energy, sustainability, biotechnology, health, or related fields. The research should prioritize materials discovery for a broad range of applications including but not limited to catalysis, membranes, soft matter and biomaterials. Candidates are expected to establish a vigorous externally funded research program and contribute to interdisciplinary collaborations across the university.
Candidates pursuing either fundamental advances in artificial intelligence or transformative applications of AI to chemical, materials, and/or manufacturing systems are encouraged to apply.
Immigration/visa sponsorship may be available in limited situations, but all decisions concerning immigration/visa sponsorship will depend on an evaluation of complexity and risk. We will not engage in immigration sponsorship for this position for individuals subject to the J-1 two-year home residency requirement or who will require consular processing for a visa to come to the United States to begin work at the university.
AI at The Ohio State University
AI is reshaping education and research, and Ohio State is at the forefront of this transformation, unlocking exponential possibilities when AI is fused with different fields. The university is committed to excellence in artificial intelligence and advancing the university’s role as a national and global leader in AI-driven discovery, education, and societal impact. In support of this commitment, Ohio State will hire 100 new tenure-track faculty with expertise in artificial intelligence (AI) over five years to drive innovation and create a central hub, the AI(X) Hub, to provide resources and foster collaboration.
This university-wide hub will span 15 colleges and unlock the exponential possibilities that emerge when AI is fused with expertise across six strategic pillars (X): foundations, health, engineering and sciences, agriculture, cybersecurity, and trustworthy AI. The AI(X) Hub will cultivate an innovation ecosystem where cross-disciplinary synergies fuel breakthroughs with profound societal impact by:
Creating a dynamic intellectual hub to harness Ohio State’s vast expertise where AI scientists and domain experts across the university can collaborate to accelerate groundbreaking research and transformative innovation
Advancing fundamental AI research to push the boundaries of AI
Establishing a collaborative hub that unites researchers, entrepreneurs, and industry leaders
Developing cutting-edge AI products that reach billions and drive meaningful change
Delivering solutions to the world’s most pressing challenges
Empowering the next generation of AI leaders through accessible AI education, mentorship, and skill development for all Ohio State learners
In addition to the AI(X) Hub, three AI Faculty Cohorts have been created: Foundational AI, Applied AI and Responsible AI and Cybersecurity. The Foundational AI Cohort will primarily focus on elevating the theoretical, mathematical and algorithmic underpinnings of AI. The Applied AI Cohort will primarily focus on harnessing AI to revolutionize the translation of ideas to real-world solutions for Ohio and beyond. The Responsible AI and Cybersecurity Cohort will primarily focus on ensuring ethical innovation and safeguarding digital landscapes for a secure future.
Position Overview
This is a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor. The successful candidate will establish an internationally recognized and externally funded research program that advances artificial intelligence and its integration with engineering and scientific discovery. The faculty member will contribute to the education of undergraduate and graduate students, participate in interdisciplinary initiatives spanning engineering and data science, and engage in service activities that support the missions of the departments, college, and university.
Performance Objectives
The candidate will be expected to help further our mission of educating undergraduate and graduate students in CBE and MSE, encouraging the exchange of ideas, methods, and insights between different fields of study, advancing the state-of-the-art knowledge in CBE, MSE, and allied fields through novel and sustained research, serving the public, academic, and industrial communities through consultation, collaborative efforts, dissemination of research results, entrepreneurship, or participation in conferences of professional societies, and valuing different perspectives.
Additional Information
The final offer for this position will be determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Salary and start-up packages are negotiated by the department chair and may vary depending on individual circumstances.
Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits packag
For questions regarding this position, please contact Nicholas Brunelli at brunelli.2@osu.edu.
Application review:
Review of applications will begin by November 1st, 2026.
Department Information
The William G. Lowrie Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (CBE) is home to 30 faculty working in diverse research areas including bioengineering, reaction engineering and catalysis, separations, systems engineering, particulates and multiphase flows, colloids, molecular simulation, polymers, nanomaterials, and sustainability. We are housed in a state-of-the-art 225,000 ft2 building dedicated to Chemical Engineering and the Chemical Sciences. CBE offers undergraduate (B.S.) and graduate (M.S. and Ph.D.) programs, with total enrollment around 900 students. CBE faculty are highly regarded for their teaching, research, and extension and outreach programs.
The Department of Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) is home to approximately 35 faculty working in diverse research areas including structural materials, electronic and photonic materials, biomaterials, energy materials, computational materials science, materials characterization, nanomaterials, welding engineering, and advanced manufacturing. MSE offers undergraduate (B.S.), master's (M.S.), and doctoral (Ph.D.) degree programs and supports a vibrant community of undergraduate and graduate students engaged in cutting-edge research. Faculty benefit from access to extensive shared research facilities and interdisciplinary collaborations across the university, including strengths in manufacturing, energy, health, data science, and artificial intelligence. MSE faculty are internationally recognized for excellence in research, teaching, and service.
The College of Engineering
Faculty Development: The Ohio State University and the College of Engineering are committed to support and develop faculty as well as the work-life balance of its faculty. These resources include The Engineering Faculty Mentoring Program, the Better Research through Better Mentoring program, and an institutional membership to the Center for the Integration of Research, Teaching and Learning. To learn more visit: https://engineering.osu.edu/faculty-development.
Learn more about the College of Engineering, the university and Columbus here.
The University
Ohio State is a top-20 public university, and its Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is one of America’s leading academic health centers. Eligible Ohio State employees receive comprehensive benefits packages, including medical, dental and vision insurance, tuition assistance for employees and their dependents, and state or alternative retirement options with competitive employer contributions.
Grounded in Ohio State University’s Shared Values, our university community welcomes differences, encourages open-minded exploration and courageous thinking, and upholds freedom of expression.
Ohio State is a dynamic community where opportunity thrives, and individuals transform themselves and their world. Positions are available in countless fields and specialties. Become a Buckeye and contribute to an incredible legacy that serves to guide our future and shape a better tomorrow.
The Ohio State University is committed to enhancing academic excellence. Recruiting, supporting, and retaining faculty of the highest caliber is a core component of this commitment. The Office of Academic Affairs (OAA) has established central resources to focus on offering support to new and prospective faculty and their loved ones. Service offerings include dual career partner consultation, potential employer and/or employment opportunity identification, consultation and resources related to relocation, as well as identifying opportunities to engage on campus and in the surrounding community. While employment opportunities are not guaranteed, resources and consultation are available. More information about dual career and faculty recruitment can be found here.
In addition to being responsive to dual-career opportunities, we strongly promote work-life balance to support our community members through a suite of institutionalized policies. Ohio State is a member of the Michigan, Ohio, Western Pennsylvania & West Virginia HERC.
Located in Ohio’s capital city, Ohio State’s Columbus campus is near the center of a rapidly growing and vibrant metropolitan area with a population of over 1.5 million. The area offers a wide range of affordable housing, many cultural and recreational opportunities, excellent schools, and a strong economy based on government as well as service, transportation, and technology industries. Additional information about the Columbus area is available here. Beyond its Columbus campus, Ohio State has four regional campuses including Ohio State Lima, Ohio State Mansfield, Ohio State Marion, and Ohio State Newark, in addition to the College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences (CFAES) Wooster Campus, which houses Ohio State ATI.
The university is an equal opportunity employer, including veterans and disability.

jobs.title: Research Associate for CROWN  Study
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: School of Nursing
jobs.description:
The Research Associate will support the NIH-funded CROWN (Cardiovascular Research Outreach through Women’s Networks). CROWN is a cluster-randomized implementation trial of a salon-based, multilevel intervention to improve blood pressure control among women in beauty salons. The intervention combines trained “Heart Health Stylists,” home blood pressure monitoring with a mobile App, community health worker, and clinical pharmacist support to improve blood pressure control.
Key responsibilities:
Coordinate day-to-day study operations, including salon partner onboarding and participant recruitment, enrollment, retention, and follow-up.
Develop and maintain the study protocol, manual of procedures, IRB submissions, and regulatory documentation.
Support training and fidelity monitoring of Heart Health Stylists and community health workers.
Oversee data collection, REDCap database management, home blood pressure data, and data quality assurance.
Conduct quantitative and qualitative analyses, including implementation outcomes, and contribute to manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and grant applications.
Build and sustain relationships with salon owners, community organizations, and clinical partners.
Supervise and mentor research assistants and students, and prepare progress reports for the sponsor.

jobs.title: Part-time Lecturer in Museum Studies
jobs.institution: Tufts University: Museum Studies Program
jobs.description:
The Museum Studies Program at Tufts University seeks one or more part‐time lecturer(s) to teach two graduate-level courses, Exhibition Planning for Art Museums and Museum Management: Leadership, Fundraising, and Administration, in Spring 2027. We invite applications from candidates interested in teaching both or only one of these courses. Museum Studies courses typically meet once per week, 6:00 - 9:00 p.m. on Tufts’ Medford campus, but there may be flexibility with scheduling.
Museum Management: Leadership, Fundraising, and Administration will provide an introduction to the core administrative responsibilities of museum staff at all levels: fundraising, budgeting, communications and marketing, event organizing, staff management, HR and legal issues, planning, and different forms of evaluation. Students will gain an understanding of key business and administrative skills essential to modern museum work. Ultimately, a museum’s ability to steward and interpret its collection, serve its community, and fulfil its mission depends on how well it is run.
Exhibition Planning for Art Museums will provide an in-depth understanding of how art curators conceive, research, organize, and stage exhibitions of all varieties, in museums of varying size, since the museum exhibition is the chief way the public experiences works of art. In an encyclopedic art museum, what are the differences between a special exhibition and an ongoing installation? How do museums organize traveling exhibitions? A single-artist exhibition and a group show? How does one work with living artists and artist-curators?

jobs.title: Research Associate for iTHRIVE Study
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: School of Nursing
jobs.description:
The Research Associate will support the iTHRIVE study. iTHRIVE is a Food Is Medicine intervention to improve blood pressure among adults with hypertension. It integrates an AI-enhanced Food Is Medicine solution, dietitian coaching, and culturally tailored adaptive messaging, and builds on the THRIVE pilot trial.
Key responsibilities:
Coordinate day-to-day study operations, including participant recruitment, enrollment, retention, and follow-up at community sites.
Develop and maintain the study protocol, manual of procedures, IRB submissions, and regulatory documentation.
Coordinate intervention delivery with dietitians, the online produce marketplace and delivery partners, and the text-messaging platform, and monitor fidelity.
Oversee data collection, REDCap database management, blood pressure and dietary data
Conduct quantitative and qualitative analyses and contribute to manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and grant applications.
Build and sustain relationships with food and produce partners, community organizations, and clinical partners.
Supervise and mentor research assistants and students, and prepare progress reports for the sponsor.

jobs.title: Adjunct Clinical Lecturer - NUR 791 - Care of Persons Across the Life Span Psychiatric Mental Health Concerns for Advanced Practice Professionals - Practicum III (Winter 2027) School of Nursing (Hybrid)
jobs.institution: University of Michigan-Flint: School of Nursing
jobs.description:
Course Description: Guided and supervised by clinical and faculty preceptors, students continue to advance diagnostic and critical-thinking skills working with clients across the life span experienceing acute and chronic mental health problems and psychiatric disorders. Students demonstrate knowledge of pharmacologic agents based on individual characteristics and conduct individual psycho-social therapy, Prerequisities are NUR 753, NUR 780, NUR 781, abd NUR 790; and consent of Program Director.
Faculty will supervise this precepted clinical via a mixed-mode format. Winter semester begins on January 6, 2027 and this course offers at 30% effort. Graded: ABCDE
Flint School of Nursing: Nursing in the 21st Century - Recent Statistics
The nursing profession has grown to nearly 5.2 million registered nurses (RNs), solidifying its position as the largest segment of the nation's healthcare workforce.
In its 2025 rankings, U.S. News & World Report named Nurse Practitioner the #1 Best Job overall, highlighting the profession's excellent future prospects, high salary potential, and stability. The Registered Nurse position ranked #54 in the same overall report and #18 in the Best Healthcare Jobs category.
According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Occupational Outlook Handbook, the employment of RNs is projected to grow 5% from 2024 to 2034, which is faster than the average for all occupations.
The Bureau also projects that the employment of nurse practitioners, nurse anesthetists, and nurse midwives will grow 40% between 2024 and 2034, much faster than the average.
The nursing profession is pivotal to advancing healthcare by addressing key issues like health equity, navigating an increasingly digitalized medical landscape, and adapting to the demands of an aging population.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow - Neutron scattering of confined fluids
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
jobs.description: An exciting postdoctoral opportunity is available in the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at Johns Hopkins University to investigate the structure and dynamics of confined fluids using neutron and X-ray scattering, complemented by techniques such as thermodynamics measurements, electron microscopy and broadband dielectric spectroscopy. The research aims to advance our understanding of both classical and quantum fluids by elucidating how atomic and molecular dynamics, dimensionality, and confinement govern their macroscopic properties.

jobs.title: Clinical Assistant Professor of Nursing
jobs.institution: Saint Mary's College: Nursing Science
jobs.description: This faculty hire will be responsible for teaching the psychiatric/mental health nursing course in both the BSN and MSN programs. Faculty members are expected to participate in curricular improvement, contribute to program assessment and accreditation activites. Candidates will also be expected to be involved in service to the department and the college community.

jobs.title: General Surgeon, Clinical Associate (Transition to Practice) #SUR198
jobs.institution: The University of Chicago: Section of General Surgery
jobs.description:
The University of Chicago’s Department of Surgery, Section of Minimally Invasive Surgery, seeks a full-time Clinical Associate. This is a one-year non-renewable transitional training position for an individual who has completed general surgery residency and seeks additional operative experience and mentorship before independent practice or fellowship. The position provides broad exposure to general surgery, including elective and acute care cases, with graduated autonomy in the operating room and clinic. The practice location for this position will primarily be within the southern suburbs at the UChicago Medicine Ingalls Memorial Hospital and in Hyde Park. This position does not require teaching or scholarly activity. Compensation is dependent upon qualifications. This position is benefits-eligible. The University of Chicago offers a wide range of benefits programs and resources for eligible employees, including health, retirement, and paid time off. Information about the benefit offerings can be found in the Benefits Guidebook.
The University of Chicago Medicine has been at the forefront of medical care since 1927. Located in historic Hyde Park, the primary medical campus includes the Center for Care and Discovery, Comer Children’s Hospital, Bernard A. Mitchell Hospital for adult inpatient care, and the Duchossois Center for Advanced Medicine (DCAM) totaling more than 550 beds in service and net patient care revenues over $1.4 billion. New ambulatory facilities are located in Orland Park and River East, and the Ingalls Health System has recently been integrated into the network.
The Section of Minimally Invasive Surgery is committed to medical education, research, patient care, and serving our community.
Prior to the start of employment, qualified applicants must: 1) have a medical doctorate or equivalent, 2) hold or be eligible for medical licensure in the State of Illinois, and 3) be Board certified or eligible in General Surgery or equivalent.
To be considered, those interested must apply through The University of Chicago’s Academic Recruitment job board, which uses Interfolio to accept applications: https://apply.interfolio.com/194288. Applicants must upload a CV and a cover letter. Review of applications will begin after October 4, 2026.
For instructions on the Interfolio application process, please visit http://tiny.cc/InterfolioHelp.

jobs.title: Clinical Psychiatrist – Psychiatric Emergency Services & Consultation-Liaison
jobs.institution: NYU Grossman School of Medicine: FGP
jobs.description:
NYU Langone Hospital–Suffolk is seeking a Clinical Psychiatrist to provide high-quality psychiatric care within Psychiatric Emergency Services (PES) and Consultation-Liaison services. The psychiatrist will evaluate and treat patients, develop treatment plans, collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, and support the delivery of safe, evidence-based care.
Key Responsibilities
Provide comprehensive psychiatric evaluation, diagnosis, treatment, and disposition of patients.
Develop and implement individualized treatment plans and ensure timely clinical documentation.
Collaborate with patients, families, healthcare professionals, and community or institutional partners as appropriate.
Participate in multidisciplinary, departmental, and hospital meetings and initiatives.
Contribute to quality improvement, regulatory compliance, and program development.
Teach and supervise medical students, residents, and other trainees.
Maintain CME and hospital medical staff requirements.
Participate in Medicare and applicable insurance plans as required.
Why Join Us
Join NYU Langone Health, a nationally recognized academic medical center committed to excellence in patient care, education, and research.
Practice in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment with opportunities to teach and mentor trainees.
Work within an integrated health system with access to a broad range of clinical and academic resources.
Enjoy the opportunity to practice on Long Island, offering proximity to New York City while providing a diverse community-based clinical setting.
Qualifications
MD or DO from an accredited medical school.
Completion of an accredited Psychiatry residency.
New York State medical license.
Board eligible or board certified in Psychiatry.
Strong clinical, communication, and organizational skills.
Compensation: $275,000-$300,000
The salary range listed is for full-time employment and does not include incentive compensation or benefits. Actual salary may not fall within the listed salary range; consideration will be made for experience, training, hospital/community need, and other factors.

jobs.title: Seaver College Faculty Fellows Program (AY26-27)
jobs.institution: Pepperdine University: Seaver College
jobs.description:
The Seaver College Faculty Fellows program seeks to advance Pepperdine University’s mission by providing one-year fellowships to individuals pursuing careers in Christian higher education and who are active members in congregations affiliated with the Churches of Christ.
The Churches of Christ are a specific tradition within the Stone-Campbell movement, and affiliation with this movement is a non-negotiable requirement of this particular position. Should applicants have any questions about this requirement, they should reach out to the associate dean listed below to discuss before submitting an application.
Pepperdine University is a Christian University committed to the highest standards of academic excellence and Christian values. Located on the University’s 830-acre campus overlooking the Pacific Ocean in Malibu, Seaver College is home to the University’s residential undergraduate program. Seaver College enjoys a national and international reputation for the quality of its programs. The College’s faculty are deeply committed to student-development, teaching, and scholarship and share a common devotion to Christian moral and ethical values. It is the purpose of Pepperdine University to pursue the very highest academic standards within a context that celebrates and extends the spiritual and ethical ideals of the Christian faith.
Part of Pepperdine's distinction is the way it values its diverse faculty, staff and student body, as well as its specific affiliation with Churches of Christ. In order to affirm its heritage, Pepperdine reserves the right to seek, hire and promote persons who support the goals and mission of the institution, including special consideration for qualified individuals who are active members in a Church of Christ congregation. Pepperdine is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of any status or condition protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
Participants in the Faculty Fellows program will develop as Christian educators by participating in the college’s academic life including programming provided by the University’s Center for Faith and Learning and the college’s Center for Teaching Excellence. Fellows will also participate in the college’s new faculty orientation, retreat, and mentoring. Fellows will teach two courses each semester and one summer-session course in an academic area of the college. Fellows will be expected to maintain an active scholarly agenda and contribute to the University through service.
For the 2026-2027 academic year, applications will be accepted from individuals who have completed a doctoral (or terminal) degree in the past three years or who have completed all course requirements and are in the dissertation phase of their doctoral studies.
The salary for this appointment will range from $70,000 to $74,000 and reflects what Pepperdine University reasonably expects to pay for this faculty appointment. Actual salary may vary based on the qualifications and experience of the applicant, as well as market conditions. In addition to salary, Pepperdine offers a robust suite of employee benefits.
Please submit all application materials by clicking [APPLY NOW]. Review of applications will begin in November 2025 and continue until the position is filled. A background check will be required as a condition of employment.
Contact:
Dr. Kindy Pfremmer De Long (kindy.delong@pepperdine.edu)
Search Committee Chair
Seaver College, Pepperdine University
24255 Pacific Coast Highway
Malibu, CA 90263
Qualified individuals should be able to show respect for workplace differences, and have the ability to work effectively with individuals from different backgrounds.
Offers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of a criminal, education, and employment screening. The University conducts such screenings in compliance with applicable laws and with the objectives of evaluating risk and supporting a safe environment for students, faculty, staff, and guests; safeguarding key University assets including people, property, information, and the University’s reputation; and providing comprehensive job-related information to University leaders to enable them to make prudent hiring decisions. Qualified individuals with criminal histories will be considered for employment in compliance with applicable laws, including the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.institution: Yale University: Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Reproductive Sciences
jobs.description: The Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Reproductive Sciences at Yale School of Medicine seeks an outstanding candidate focusing on minimally invasive gynecologic surgery (MIGS) at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor. jobs.institution: NYU Grossman School of Medicine: Pediatrics
jobs.description:
The Division of Pediatric Rheumatology at the Hassenfeld Children’s Hospital at NYU Langone Health is seeking a board certified/board eligible pediatric rheumatologist for a faculty position. Our team is expanding and this individual will join our collaborative team dedicated to providing comprehensive care for children with a broad range of rheumatologic conditions.
The Division of Pediatric Rheumatology provides specialized care for patients with conditions including juvenile idiopathic arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, vasculitis, dermatomyositis, autoinflammatory syndromes, uveitis and other inflammatory disorders. The division works closely with colleagues across pediatric subspecialties to deliver multidisciplinary, family-centered care tailored to the needs of each patient. The division also works closely with the adult rheumatology division, participating in all didactics, as well as training adult rheumatology fellows.
Responsibilities include comprehensive outpatient and inpatient clinical care, consultation services, teaching of fellows, medical students, and pediatric residents, and participation in hospital-related administrative, research, and/or quality improvement initiatives. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the academic mission of the Department of Pediatrics through education, scholarly activity, and clinical excellence.
Applicants are eligible for a faculty appointment at NYU Grossman School of Medicine, Department of Pediatrics. NYU Langone Health offers a competitive salary and benefits and is an equal opportunity employer; we encourage inquiry from applicants of diverse backgrounds.
Salary Range: $190,000- $210,000
The salary range listed is for full-time employment and does not include incentive compensation or benefits. Actual salary may not fall within the listed salary range; consideration will be made for experience, training, hospital/community need, and other factors.
Qualifications
The ideal candidate will be BC/BE in Pediatric Rheumatology, possess outstanding clinical skills, and be committed to participating in fellow, resident, and medical student education, as well as scholarly activities.
Application Instructions
Please submit your letter of intent addressed to the Director of the Division of Pediatric Rheumatology and CV through our online application portal, Interfolio. If you have questions, please contact Lauren Paletti at Lauren.Paletti@nyulangone.org.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
NYU Langone Health is an equal opportunity employer and committed to inclusion in all aspects of recruiting and employment. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Pediatric at CUMC -Newborn Nursery
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Pediatrics
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY/POSITION DESCRIPTION
This opportunity to join the Department of Pediatrics at the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons at the rank of Assistant Professor is an exciting one. Columbia University Irving Medical Center, one of the nation’s foremost academic health science center’s working together with one of the nation’s premier health systems, New York-Presbyterian Hospital.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Provide timely and high-quality care to healthy newborns in the busy well-baby nursery, located at Columbia University Irving Medical Center/Morgan Stanley Children’s Hospital.
· Provide comprehensive medical evaluation and management of healthy and medically complex newborns in the Well Baby Nursery, delivering evidence-based, family-centered care from admission through hospital discharge.
· Admit, evaluate, and discharge newborn patients, including conducting admission histories and physical examinations, developing and implementing treatment plans, coordinating discharge readiness, and ensuring appropriate outpatient follow-up.
· Provide clinical coverage for the Well Baby Nursery on a rotating schedule, including weekdays, weekends, holidays, and shared call responsibilities, to ensure continuous physician coverage and timely evaluation and management of newborn patients.
· Perform daily newborn rounds and manage common neonatal conditions, including feeding difficulties, hyperbilirubinemia, hypoglycemia, neonatal abstinence syndrome, and other conditions requiring close monitoring or intervention.
· Collaborate with obstetric, maternal-fetal medicine, neonatal intensive care, nursing, lactation, social work, and pediatric subspecialty teams to ensure coordinated, multidisciplinary care and seamless transitions throughout the newborn hospitalization.
· Educate and counsel parents and caregivers regarding newborn health, breastfeeding and nutrition, safe sleep practices, immunizations, routine newborn screening, and discharge instructions to support a safe transition to outpatient pediatric care.
· Teach and supervise trainees in the clinical care of newborns, while participating in quality improvement initiatives, patient safety programs, and scholarly activities that advance the clinical, educational, and research missions of the Department of Pediatrics.
commitment of diversity

The University is dedicated to the goal of building a culturally diverse and pluralistic faculty and staff committed to teaching and working in a diverse environment, and strongly encourages applications from women, minorities, individuals with disabilities, and veterans.
Columbia University welcomes applications from individuals who may have had nontraditional career paths, or who may have taken time off for family reasons (e.g. children, caring for disabled or elderly family), or who have achieved excellence in careers outside of academia (e.g., in professional or industry service). We are interested in candidates who have a record of success advising and mentoring individuals from groups underrepresented in higher education and is particularly interested in candidates who have research interests in subjects that will contribute to the understanding of diversity and equal opportunity.

jobs.description:
Tenure-Track Assistant Professor
Architecture Section / Knowlton School of Architecture
The Architecture Section of the Knowlton School at The Ohio State University (OSU) welcomes applications for two (2) tenure-track faculty positions, starting as early as Autumn 2027. We seek candidates whose expertise will complement and expand the Knowlton School’s dynamic faculty, contributing to a rich culture of design, history and theory, technology, and contemporary architectural practice. Selected candidates will teach across the undergraduate and graduate architecture curricula, with teaching roles tailored to their areas of expertise and research. Candidates should be capable of leading design studios at the undergraduate and graduate levels, as well as teaching lecture courses, seminars, and/or other forms of instruction depending on their specialization.
We are interested in energetic, intellectually curious, and creative colleagues with an ambitious research agenda. As architecture confronts profound changes in climate, technology, urbanization, and modes of production, we welcome candidates whose work engages critically and imaginatively with the contemporary moment. Rather than prescribing a particular subject area or mode of practice, we are especially interested in research and teaching that open new questions for the discipline and expand how architecture might understand and act upon the conditions in which it operates.
Potential research and teaching themes may include –– but are not limited to:
Critical approaches to architectural design and engaged practice
Architecture’s engagement with contemporary social and environmental conditions
Changing forms of urbanization, infrastructure, and settlement
Emerging materials, technologies, and modes of construction
Other areas of inquiry that introduce perspectives, methods, or problems not currently represented within the Architecture Section
Position Overview
This position will be appointed at the rank of tenure-track Assistant Professor. Candidates should demonstrate strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work both independently and collegially. Successful candidates will bring initiative, intellectual openness, and a willingness to contribute constructively to the academic community.
Immigration/visa sponsorship may be available in very limited situations, but all decisions concerning immigration/visa sponsorship will depend on an evaluation of complexity and risk. We will not engage in immigration sponsorship for this position for individuals subject to the J-1 two-year home residency requirement or who will require consular processing for a visa to come to the United States to begin work at the university.

Demonstrate high-quality and inclusive teaching; contribute to curricular development; and advise and mentor graduate and undergraduate students;
Develop an original and coherent program of scholarly and/or creative work; disseminate that work through recognized public venues; and demonstrate sustained productivity, disciplinary contribution, and growing national/international recognition.
Contribute collegially to school governance, recruitment, faculty activities, and appropriate professional, university, or civic service.
Demonstrate continuing growth and high-quality performance across teaching, scholarship, and service, documented through annual reviews, with mandatory tenure review normally occurring in year six.

jobs.institution: The Ohio State University: Knowlton School of Architecture
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor Knowlton School / Landscape Architecture
College of Engineering
The Landscape Architecture Section of the Ohio State University’s Knowlton School invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor. Located in one of the fastest-growing metropolitan regions in the US, the landscape architecture program pursues urban pasts, presents, and futures through highly engaged, design-centered, and future-oriented curricula while fostering individual research trajectories. To join us in that pursuit, we seek a colleague whose research and creative practice explore emerging technologies and their implications for landscape architecture, with particular interest in work engaging urban environments and ecologies.
This position will start as early as August of 2027.
Position Overview
The Knowlton School is a tenure-initiating unit within the College of Engineering housing sections in architecture, landscape architecture, and city and regional planning. With 45 faculty members, 750 students, and 15 staff members, the Knowlton School forms a distinct community that fosters inquiry and exchange across sections, the college, and the university, as well as Ohio and Midwestern communities at large. Cross-disciplinary teaching and research are highly valued, and innovation is encouraged.
Founded by the eminent modernist AD Taylor in 1915, the Landscape Architecture section at Knowlton is one of the oldest landscape architecture programs in the US. Our faculty currently comprises thirteen full-time collegial and collaborative scholars dedicated to advancing the work, disciplinary questions, and practice of landscape architecture. We offer fully accredited degrees at both the graduate (master's) and undergraduate level with roughly 30 students in the graduate program and 120 in the undergraduate program.
The Landscape Architecture section is also home to the Midwest Landscape Lab, a research platform supporting collaborative, place-based inquiry into the ecological, material, and cultural futures of Midwestern landscapes. The Lab offers opportunities to extend research in emerging technologies through interdisciplinary collaboration, applied research, and engagement with the region’s landscapes and communities.
For this tenure-track assistant professor-level position, we seek a colleague whose research and creative practice advance the role of emerging technologies in landscape architecture, with a particular interest in work that engages urban environments and ecologies. Scholarship may take the form of research, applied research, creative practice, professional work, or hybrid forms of inquiry and dissemination. We are particularly interested in candidates whose work expands the methods and media through which landscape architecture is researched, represented, designed, and constructed.
This is a full-time position. The selected candidate will be expected to teach a standard portfolio of 2 courses per academic semester (4 courses per academic year) at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. Teaching is a respected and highly valued component of a tenure-track position, and prior teaching experience in your area of expertise is highly desirable. The selected candidate will also be expected to contribute to student mentoring and development. This hire will have the opportunity to reshape parts of the undergraduate and graduate curricula and is expected to bring their research agenda to bear on significant portions of their teaching. The section and school value collaboration and team teaching, and welcome collaborative development of new courses within the section or across the school, college, or university.
Tenure-track Assistant Professors are expected to develop a significant body of work around their area of scholarship. At Ohio State, externally recognized creative and professional scholarship is acknowledged alongside peer-reviewed publication as a legitimate path toward tenure. As a section and school, we highly value collaboration, and you will find a community willing to collaborate on grants and projects. Ample mentoring opportunities exist within the section, school, and college of engineering, and successful candidates will be expected and encouraged to tap the abundant resources offered by one of the largest R1 universities in the US.
All tenure-track faculty are expected to serve at the section, school, and college levels, and service is essential for promotion.
Immigration/visa sponsorship may be available in very limited situations, but all decisions concerning immigration/visa sponsorship will depend on an evaluation of complexity and risk. We will not engage in immigration sponsorship for this position for individuals subject to the J-1 two-year home residency requirement or who will require consular processing for a visa to come to the United States to begin work at the university.
Performance Objectives:
Time within this position is split 60% teaching, 30% research, and 10% service
The successful candidate will teach four courses per academic year divided between Fall and Spring Semesters. Typically, two courses per semester, with course leave and buyouts possible for special projects or opportunities at the discretion of the section-head and director. Demonstrated commitment to teaching and mentoring is a crucial component of tenure at Ohio State.
Tenure-track faculty are expected to develop a significant, recognized body of scholarship during their probationary period.
As a tenure-track position, mandatory tenure reviews will be conducted at the 4th year and 6th year.
The awarding of tenure and promotion to the rank of Associate Professor is based upon clear and convincing evidence that the candidate has provided and will continue to provide high-quality teaching, scholarship, and service relevant to the mission of the school.
Additional Information
The final offer for this position will be determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Salary and start-up packages are negotiated by the director and may vary depending on individual circumstances.
Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.
For questions regarding this position, please contact Search Committee Chair Jake Boswell at 614-688-4586 / boswell.33@osu.edu.

The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering is one of the largest departments in the College of Engineering at The Ohio State University. Design and synthesis of new amino acid analogues
Preparation of oligonucleotide derivatives of these amino acid analogues
Purification and characterization of the peptides and proteins created in in vitro, and in vivo biochemical systems.

jobs.institution: Arizona State University: Biodesign Center for Bioenergetics
jobs.description:
The Arizona State University's Biodesign Center for BioEnergetics and Professor Sidney Hecht invite applications for a Postdoctoral Research Scholar to assist with biochemical aspects of the biosynthesis of proteins containing non-proteinogenic amino acids. Design of modified peptides and proteins
Preparation of peptides and proteins containing non-canonical amino acids
Purification, characterization and study of the proteins created in in vitro and in vivo biochemical systems.

jobs.location: School of Medicine and Dentistry Room G8011

The Department of Health Humanities & Bioethics in the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry (URSMD) seeks to recruit a faculty member (open rank) for a tenure eligible position in Health Humanities & Bioethics with specific focus on ELSI genetics, neuroethics, AI ethics, or research ethics.

jobs.title: Junior Faculty Fellowship in Ethics
jobs.institution: Georgetown University: Strategy
jobs.description:
The Georgetown Institute for the Study for Markets and Ethics at Georgetown University's McDonough School of Business seeks applications for a Junior Faculty Fellowship in Ethics. As part of its mission to advance scholarship and the teaching of ethics in universities and professional schools, the Institute offers Junior Faculty Fellowships in Ethics to new PhDs or recent PhDs in non-tenure track positions who wish to pursue a career teaching and researching applied ethics. This is a one-year fellowship.
The fellowship is open to recent PhDs in normative disciplines such as philosophy, political science, and public policy, as well as to recent law graduates who hold a PhD in a cognate field. Compensation is highly competitive. Appointment is for the period August 1, 2027, to July 31, 2028.
We have one opening for the 2027-2028 academic year. This fellowship is designed to provide the training and experience essential to becoming a successful university-level teacher of applied ethics. GISME Junior Fellows teach two sections of an ethics course per year in either MSB or Georgetown’s philosophy department, collaborate with GISME faculty on other courses, and receive the support of Georgetown's ethics faculty to produce quality scholarship during their time in residence. Fellows also participate in GISME’s academic symposia and its ongoing project to develop innovative tools and techniques to improve the teaching of applied and professional ethics. Fellows are required to produce at least one article of publishable quality during the term of the fellowship.
ABOUT GEORGETOWN UNIVERSITY’s MCDONOUGH SCHOOL OF BUSINESS
Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business offers unparalleled access to the world's business, policy, and thought leaders. The school, which attracts faculty and students from around the world, is committed to building global business knowledge and inspiring ethical leaders to serve the common good. Known for its emphasis at the intersection of business and global affairs and its values-based approach to business as part of Georgetown's rich Catholic, Jesuit tradition, the school also is focused on how business can be a force for change by addressing fields of the future, such as healthcare, sustainability, and AI and the future of work. The school's undergraduate and graduate degree programs provide solid grounding in all the core management disciplines, with an emphasis on the global, ethical, and political environment of business. The McDonough School of Business has an ongoing commitment to being a community in diversity as a fundamental aspect of the Georgetown community.

All applications should be submitted electronically to Interfolio. Please send only a CV or resume and a cover letter describing one's teaching and research interests. You can submit questions about this position to Michael Douma at mjd289@georgetown.edu.
Deadline for applications is February 15, 2027
The projected salary or hourly pay range for this position is $75,000-$100,000. Compensation is determined by a number of factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s individual qualifications, experience, education, skills, and certifications, as well as the University’s business needs and external factors.

jobs.description:
The Department of Industrial and Operations Engineering (IOE) at the University of Michigan (U-M) welcomes applications for a faculty position at any rank (assistant, associate, or full professor) in all areas related to IOE, including human factors and ergonomics, operations research, and data analytics. Of particular interest are candidates whose research intersects with artificial intelligence (AI), broadly defined, and emerging technologies in sociotechnical systems. An ideal candidate will have a strong methodological emphasis (drawing on fields such as applied probability, computation, neuroscience, optimization, psychology, statistics, and social sciences) and a significant engagement with applications, including but not limited to advanced manufacturing, business operations, energy systems, healthcare, human-systems integration, and transportation.
Senior candidates are expected to have a track record of excellence in both research as well as graduate and undergraduate education and have a demonstrated ability to establish independent and externally-funded research programs in their fields of expertise. Particular attention will be placed on candidates who embrace the global outlook, leadership focus, and service commitment that are fundamental to the culture of Michigan Engineering.
Who We Are:
Michigan Engineering provides scientific and technological leadership to the people of the world. We seek to improve the quality of life by developing intellectually curious and socially conscious minds, creating collaborative solutions to societal problems, and promoting an inclusive and innovative community of service for the common good. The College of Engineering is especially interested in candidates who can contribute, through their research, teaching and/or service, to the diversity and excellence of the academic community.
Michigan Engineering’s vision is to be the world’s preeminent college of engineering serving the common good. This global outlook, leadership focus, and service commitment permeate our culture. Our vision is supported by a mission and values that, together, provide the framework for all that we do. Information about our vision, mission and values can be found at: http://strategicvision.engin.umich.edu/.
The IOE Department is a nationally recognized leader in education and research focused on improving complex systems through data analytics, human systems integration, optimization, and stochastic systems. IOE brings together outstanding faculty, students, and collaborators to address consequential challenges across areas such as business operations, energy and sustainability, health and human safety, and mobility and transportation networks. The department has a longstanding record of excellence and is consistently ranked among the top industrial engineering programs in the nation; in the 2026 U.S. News & World Report rankings, Michigan IOE is ranked #2 nationally for its graduate program and #3 for its undergraduate program.

Collaborate with instructional designers and full-time faculty to develop new digital forensic courses, such as, but not limited to, Digital Forensics; Advanced Digital Forensics; Multimedia Forensics; Network Forensics Analysis; Database Forensics; Mobile Forensics; and Internet of Things (IoT) Forensics, or others.

Conduct quantitative and qualitative research

jobs.title: Borders & Boundaries in World Politics Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027-2028
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: Academic Opportunities: Perry World House
jobs.description:
The Borders and Boundaries Project is concerned with boundaries between organized human communities, broadly understood. International borders, border regions and border crossings have multiple significance as designations of state authority, security buffers, expressions of social meaning and opportunities for economic integration.
Border regions and activities speak to national and local encounters with neighbors and the rest of the world. This project is concerned with how humans demarcate the space between “us” and “them.” It contextualizes border architecture, infrastructure and institutions as expressions of various social, political and economic opportunities and anxieties associated with globalization. This research team will concern itself with a broad range of questions relating to international bordering and its consequences. The project team is run by Professor Beth Simmons, Andrea Mitchell University Professor in Law, Political Science, and Business Ethics.
Research Postdoctoral Fellowship
Applicants with an interest in territorial politics; migration and movement across borders, especially in the context of climate change; development in and across border regions; border-related law and human rights, cooperation, and institutions; transnational crime, human trafficking and law enforcement across borders; and related issues are welcome to apply.
Responsibilities
The postdoctoral fellow will split their time between their own research and Borders & Boundaries project research. Postdoctoral fellows will be expected to work 25% of their time on project research. There are no mandatory teaching responsibilities. Postdoctoral fellows will be expected to give a presentation during the academic year in the Perry World House Seminar Series, engage with Perry World House’s Undergraduate Student Fellows, and attend regularly scheduled seminars. Perry World House will also introduce each postdoctoral fellow to related faculty and leaders of centers and institutes at the University of Pennsylvania.

jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Data Science Institute
jobs.description:
The position will support research within Columbia University’s Data Science Institute under the direction of Professors Kathleen McKeown and David Blei. The incumbent will conduct research focused on advancing generative modeling methods, with particular emphasis on improving search and sampling techniques and developing methods to quantify risks associated with increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems.
Research responsibilities will include developing dynamic particle-based and gradient-guided sampling methods for diffusion and autoregressive models; investigating backtracking and local exploration strategies to improve controllable generation; and examining fine-tuning approaches that incorporate improved sampling methods to enhance model efficiency and performance.
The incumbent will also investigate the comparative suitability of autoregressive and diffusion models for search tasks and develop methodologies for rare-event estimation to support the evaluation and assessment of model safety. This work will include developing sample-efficient approaches for estimating the probability of harmful or other low-frequency model outputs.
The position will work closely with Professors McKeown and Blei and collaborate with affiliated faculty, researchers, and other members of the Data Science Institute research community. The incumbent will be responsible for conducting original research, developing and evaluating research methodologies, analyzing and documenting results, and contributing to the broader research objectives of the Institute.
The incumbent will also be expected to communicate research findings through presentations at scientific meetings and conferences and through publications in leading research conferences and peer-reviewed journals. The research conducted in this position is intended to contribute to methodological advances in generative modeling and to the development of approaches that support the responsible evaluation and deployment of artificial intelligence systems in scientific and societal contexts.
